## 5.2 `ui.PlatformDispatcher`, `ui.View` and engine wiring

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.2-platform-dispatcher
- **Summary:** `ui.PlatformDispatcher` has the views, the frame callbacks (`OnBeginFrame` with times that never go back, `OnDrawFrame`), `ScheduleFrame`, the pointer packet and key data callbacks, locales, text scale factor, platform brightness, accessibility features, accent color, displays, the app lifecycle state and `RequestAppExit`. `ui.View` has its ID, physical size, device pixel ratio, padding, insets, gesture insets, constraints, display and `Render(scene) error`. `internal/engine` creates the dispatcher, adds a view for the window, and turns the platform `Handler` calls into dispatcher calls: input is queued and handed over at the start of the next frame, a frame runs `BeginFrame` then `DrawFrame`, `View.Render` goes to the renderer, and a frame in which nothing was rendered draws the last scene again so that the platform gets the one frame it asked for. `Config.Start` is where the framework will attach itself (step 7.4); the dev examples' `Config.Scene` now runs on the dispatcher.

## 7.3 Error containment, goroutines and thread checks

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.3-error-containment
- **Summary:** every recovery point of SPEC §14.2 recovers, reports and goes on, replacing the `TODO(step 7.3)` markers. `foundation` gets `ErrorReporter`, the tags `BuildPanicked`, `LayoutPanicked`, `PaintPanicked` and `CallbackPanicked`, `PanicError`, `Guard`, `IsRecoveredPanic` and `UIThread` (on `internal/goid`). The reporter is passed down by options, never global: `ChangeNotifier.NotifyListeners` (all listeners run, the first panic is reported), the scheduler (tasks, transient, persistent and post-frame callbacks), the gesture binding (packet handling, each hit test target, the pointer router, the pointer signal resolver, and every recognizer callback through `InvokeCallback`), the render objects (`PerformResize`, `PerformLayout`, `Paint`, through `DebugOptions.ReportError`), the painting binding (`PaintingBindingOpts.Reporter`, image listeners) and the widgets (`ComponentElement.PerformRebuild` puts an `ErrorWidget` made by `BuildOwnerOpts.ErrorWidgetBuilder` in place of a widget whose `Build` or whose child's creation panicked; `BuildScope.tryRebuild` reports and builds the next element). `SetState` from another goroutine posts through `BuildOwnerOpts.Post` and is dropped if the state was unmounted; `StateOf.Go(func(ctx))` runs under `Lifetime()` with the same recovery and reports on the UI thread. Debug builds report `WrongThread` in `Element.MarkNeedsBuild`, `RenderObject.MarkNeedsLayout` (`DebugOptions.UIThread`), `ChangeNotifier.NotifyListeners` and `State.Go`.
- **Main files:** `foundation/{error_report,ui_thread}.go`, `internal/goid/goid.go`, changes to `foundation/change_notifier.go`, `scheduler/binding.go`, `gestures/{binding,pointer_router,pointer_signal_resolver,recognizer}.go`, `rendering/{object,binding,debug}.go`, `painting/{binding,image_stream}.go`, `widgets/{component_element,build_owner,state,element,error_widget}.go`
- **Proof:** none (the step has no Proof item)

  - `rendering/error_containment_test.go`: a panic in `PerformLayout`, `PerformResize` and `Paint` is reported, the siblings are laid out and painted, and the frame finishes; `WrongThread` in `MarkNeedsLayout`.
  - `widgets/error_containment_test.go`: a panic in `Build` shows the `ErrorWidget` and the siblings keep working, the widget builds again when fixed; a panic in `InitState` of a child; a custom `ErrorWidgetBuilder`; no recovery without a reporter; a panic in `BuildScope.tryRebuild`. `widgets/thread_test.go`: `SetState` from 50 goroutines (one rebuild), dropped after unmount, `State.Go` recovery with a tagged and an untagged panic and the cancelled context, `StateGoBeforeMount`, `WrongThread`.

## 7.4 WidgetsBinding, RunApp and capture-on-idle

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.4-widgets-binding
- **Summary:** `widgets.RunApp(app, opts)` (and `RunWidget`) now runs a widget app: it opens the first window, makes the `WidgetsBinding` (which owns the scheduler, gesture, painting and renderer bindings, the `BuildOwner` and the root element, and hands the one error reporter and the `UIThread` to all of them), wraps the app in a `View`, and builds, lays out, paints and composites every frame. `View`/`RawView` bridge a `ui.View` to a `RenderView` and its pipeline owner; `MediaQuery` (every `MediaQueryData` field Glutter can provide, with aspects) is kept up to date from the view; `Directionality`, `AppLifecycleListener` (with `OnExitRequested`, which can keep a window open), `WidgetsBindingObserver`, the generated lifecycle transitions, `ExitApplication`, `widgets.DebugOptions` and `WidgetsBindingOf(bc)` are in. With `GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT` and no delay the engine waits until the app is idle (no frame, animation or image pending; at most 5 s) before it saves the window. `ErrorWidget` gets the text engine of the binding.
- **Main files:** `widgets/{binding,view,media_query,directionality,app_lifecycle_listener,run_app,debug_options}.go`, changes to `widgets/{build_owner,element,element_tree,error_widget}.go`; `ui/{lifecycle,platform_dispatcher}.go` (`AppExitType`, `AppExitResponse`, `OnExitRequested`, `RequestClose`, `IsIdle`), `scheduler/binding.go` (`FramesGate`), `rendering/binding.go` (`WrapDrawFrame`), `internal/engine/engine.go` (close request, capture on idle, no draw before the first configure), `internal/renderhost/renderhost.go`, `examples/dev/runapp/`.

Both backends, the capture waited for the first idle frame.

## 7.9 `examples/custompaint`

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.9-custompaint-example
- **Summary:** The second public example, `examples/custompaint`, shows `CustomPaint` with a custom painter that draws an analog clock: a shadow (`Canvas.DrawShadow`), a face with a radial gradient and a rim, 60 ticks (longer and thicker every five) drawn with `Save`, `Translate` and `Rotate`, and hour, minute and second hands with round caps and a center cap. A `StatefulWidget` (`clockApp`) updates the time every second from a goroutine started with `State.Go` that calls `SetState`; it stops when the state is disposed. The painter repaints only through `ShouldRepaint` (it is true when the second changed). The clock function is given to the widget's constructor (`newClockApp(time.Now)` in `main`, a fixed time in the tests). Window title: "Glutter – custom paint".
- **Main files:** `examples/custompaint/main.go`, `examples/custompaint/custompaint_test.go`, `examples/custompaint/testdata/goldens/clock.png`.
- **Proof:** B, `docs/implemented-proof-images/7.9-custompaint.png`, made by running the example in a headless sway session with `GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT` (the OpenGL ES renderer). It shows the clock face with the hands at 13:36:25, the time of the screenshot: the hour hand is between 1 and 2, the minute hand points at 36 minutes and the red second hand at 25 seconds. The edges of the face, the ticks and the hands are antialiased, the gradient is smooth and the shadow is below the face.
- **Tests:** 4 Go tests (6 with the table cases) in `examples/custompaint/custompaint_test.go`: a golden at 10:08:35 (which was looked at), `ShouldRepaint` (3 cases), the painter paints once for a rebuild in the same second and again for a new second (counted through a hook of the widget), and the real goroutine asks for the time again after a second and stops when the widget leaves the tree.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go test -tags glutter_release` and `-tags glutter_profile` on `./examples/...` ✅

## 8.4 `examples/animations`

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-8.4-animations-example
- **Summary:** the third public example, `examples/animations`, runs with `widgets.RunApp` and uses only public packages. Four tiles in a 2x2 grid, each with a title, the animation and the name of its curve (a `Text`): an `AnimatedContainer` that changes size, color and corner radius when tapped (`Curves.easeInOutCubic`, 600 ms); `Pulse`, a widget of the example made of a `ScaleTransition` and a controller that repeats back and forth (`easeInOut`); an `AnimatedSwitcher` that cycles a counter with a scale and fade transition (`easeOut`); and a `TweenAnimationBuilder` that turns a plus sign by a quarter turn at a time (`easeInOutBack`, 800 ms). The app starts the container, the counter and the turn by itself after 100 ms and then every two seconds (a goroutine started with `State.Go`; `autoAdvance` is false in the tests). Window title: "Glutter – animations".

All four tiles are mid-animation: the container is a rounded shape between the primary and the tertiary color, the pulse circle is scaled up, the counter shows 1, and the plus sign is turned about 45 degrees.

## 9.4 `examples/scrolling`

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-9.4-scrolling-example
- **Summary:** the fourth public example, `examples/scrolling`, runs with `widgets.RunApp` and uses only public packages. A row of five tabs (plain `GestureDetector`s on rounded boxes, since Material is not available yet) switches between: a `ListViewBuilder` with 10,000 rows of text (fixed item extent); a `GridViewCount` of 120 colored tiles; a `CustomScrollView` with a pinned `SliverPersistentHeader` (140 px shrinking to 56 px, a darker color while it overlaps content), a `SliverList` of 30 rows and a `SliverGridCount` of 18 tiles; a `PageView` of three pages; and a `ReorderableList` of twelve items with a grip drawn as three bars and a `ReorderableDragStartListener`. Each scroll view has a `ScrollController` and a `RawScrollbar` with an always visible thumb, from a `ScrollConfiguration` whose behavior overrides `BuildScrollbar`. In debug builds `GLUTTER_DEV_TAB` (0 to 4) opens a tab and `GLUTTER_DEV_SCROLL` (pixels) sets the initial offset of the `CustomScrollView` tab; release builds ignore both. Window title: "Glutter – scrolling".
- **Main files:** `examples/scrolling/main.go`, `examples/scrolling/scrolling_test.go`, `examples/scrolling/testdata/goldens/scrolling-{list,grid,custom,custom-scrolled,pages,reorder}.png`.

It shows the CustomScrollView tab scrolled by 600 px: the pinned header (56 px, darker purple) is at the top, a list row passes under it, and the scrollbar thumb is at the right edge.

  ![9.4 scrolling](implemented-proof-images/9.4-scrolling.png)
- **Tests:** 9 Go tests in `examples/scrolling/scrolling_test.go` (there is no Dart counterpart to port): a golden of each tab (six images, with the CustomScrollView tab at rest and scrolled; all looked at), the tabs switching the view, a scrollbar in every scrolling tab, a fling of the list (it keeps scrolling after the release and builds only rows near the viewport), the pinned header keeping its top and its minimum height, the PageView swiped to its last page, a reorder of the first item two places down (a drag in small steps), and the options of the environment (valid values, and the `ScrollingTabInvalid` and `ScrollingOffsetInvalid` routes; the release build ignoring them).

Found while writing the reorder test: a drag that jumps a whole row in one pointer event gives results that are not monotonic in the distance (the gap animation has not run); this is Flutter's algorithm (`_dragUpdateItems` is ported line by line), so the test moves in small steps as a hand does.

## 10.7 `examples/navigation`

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-10.7-navigation-example
- **Summary:** a runnable example of the navigation of M10 on a `WidgetsApp`, without Material. The home page has two tabs. "Imperative" opens a detail page with `NavigatorPush` and a `PageRouteBuilder` that slides in from the right; the thumbnail on the home page and the large picture on the detail page are one `Hero`, which flies between them; "Pick a color" pushes a page that pops with a value, and the home page reads it from the channel of `NavigatorPush` in a goroutine (`StateOf.Go` and `SetState`). "Pages API" keeps a stack of pages in a nested `Navigator` (`Pages`, `OnDidRemovePage`). Every link is a `FocusableActionDetector` with a thick border while it has the focus: Tab and Shift+Tab move between them, Enter and Space follow them (the `ActivateIntent` of the default shortcuts), and Escape pops (each page maps the `DismissIntent` to a pop of the nearest `Navigator`).
- **Main files:** `examples/navigation/main.go`, `examples/navigation/navigation_test.go`, `examples/navigation/testdata/goldens/`
- **Proof:** B, `docs/implemented-proof-images/10.7-navigation.png`, made by running the example in a headless sway session with `GLUTTER_DEV_ROUTE=/detail GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT=... GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT_AFTER=1s` (the OpenGL ES renderer). It shows the detail page after the slide: the large hero picture, the title and text, and the autofocused Back link with its teal focus border next to the plain Favorite link.

  ![10.7 navigation](implemented-proof-images/10.7-navigation.png)
- **Tests:** `gluttertest` tests, with the fake platform and the fake clock: the four pages against golden images (home, Pages API tab, detail, picker), a push that slides the detail page in (x between 640 and 0 mid-way, 0 at the end) and its pop with the Back link, the hero in flight and its size, the picker's result through the channel (a choice, Cancel, Escape), Tab and Shift+Tab through the links of the home page, Enter on a focused link, Escape on the home page (nothing) and on the detail page, the Favorite link with the keyboard, the stack of the Pages API tab (push twice, Back, Escape in the nested navigator), the `GLUTTER_DEV_*` variables (their tags have route tests) and their being ignored in release builds. No Dart tests are ported; the step has none.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go test -tags glutter_release` and `-tags glutter_profile` on `./examples/navigation` ✅

- **Deviations and follow-ups:** none in the framework. The example finds that the Actions of a `ModalRoute` map the `DismissIntent` to an action that is off for a page route, and that the closest mapping wins, as in Flutter (`Actions.maybeFind` stops at the first mapping): so Escape cannot be handled by one action in the `WidgetsApp`; each page provides its own, as `MaterialApp` pages do through the `Scaffold` and its buttons. The hero is a painted gradient and a circle, so that the example needs no image file.

## 11.1 D-Bus connection and settings portal

- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Branch:** feat/step-11.1-dbus-settings-portal
- **Summary:** `internal/dbus` now talks to the session bus through `github.com/godbus/dbus/v5`. `Bus` is the small interface that the services use (`Call`, `Subscribe`, `UniqueName`, `Close`); `Connect` opens the session bus (`DBusConnectFailed`) and `NewBus` wraps any connection. `PortalRequest` is the helper for portal methods that answer through an `org.freedesktop.portal.Request`: it subscribes to `Response` at the path derived from the handle token before it calls (so an answer that comes at once is kept), follows the handle of an older portal, treats Cancelled and Ended as results, and closes the request when the context is done. `ReadSettings` and `WatchSettings` read and follow the keys of SPEC §8.8 (`color-scheme`, `accent-color`, `contrast`, `text-scaling-factor`, `enable-animations`, `cursor-size`, `cursor-theme`, `font-antialiasing`, `font-hinting`) over `org.freedesktop.portal.Settings`; each change goes through `post` (`Platform.Post`) to `onSettings` (`Handler.OnSettings`), and the engine hands it to `PlatformDispatcher` (brightness, text scale, `DisableAnimations`, accessibility features). When there is no bus or no portal, `FallbackSettings` gives `XCURSOR_SIZE`, `XCURSOR_THEME` and the defaults. `platform.Settings` gained `CursorSize`, `CursorTheme`, `FontAntialiasing` and `FontHinting`. `internal/dbus/fakebus` is the in-process fake bus of SPEC §17.
- **Main files:** `internal/dbus/bus.go`, `internal/dbus/request.go`, `internal/dbus/settings.go`, `internal/dbus/values.go`, `internal/dbus/fakebus/fakebus.go`, `internal/platform/settings.go`, `go.mod`

Every tag has a route test: `DBusConnectFailed`, `DBusCallFailed`, `DBusSubscribeFailed`, `DBusCloseFailed`, `SettingsReplyInvalid`, `PortalReplyInvalid`, `PortalResponseInvalid`, `PortalRequestClosed`, `PortalRequestAborted`. ## 11.3 IME over D-Bus (X11, and Wayland without text-input-v3)

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-11.3-ime-over-dbus
- **Summary:** IBus and Fcitx5 over D-Bus, behind one `dbus.InputMethod` interface (`FocusIn`/`FocusOut`, `Reset`, `SetCursorRect`, `SetContent`, `SetSurroundingText`, `ProcessKey`), with `dbus.OpenInputMethod` choosing the framework that runs (the one named by `XMODIFIERS`, `GTK_IM_MODULE` or `QT_IM_MODULE` first, else Fcitx5, then IBus; neither is `InputMethodUnavailable`). IBus goes to the private bus of its daemon (`IBusAddress`: `IBUS_ADDRESS` or the socket file of the config directory, `ConnectAddress`) and falls back to its portal on the session bus; its text is the `IBusText` struct, its preedit cursor is in characters. Fcitx5 uses `org.fcitx.Fcitx5` or `org.freedesktop.portal.Fcitx`, `CreateInputContext(a(ss))`, capability flags from the field's purpose, formatted preedit in bytes, and the X keycode (evdev + 8). The signals become `IMEEvent` (commit, preedit, delete). `internal/platform/linux/ime.Bridge` runs the calls on a goroutine, sends only what changed (content, surrounding text in characters, caret, focus), resets the composition when the field changes by something other than the input method, hands the answers to the UI thread through the loop, and turns the events into `ui.TextInputEvent` (character counts become bytes around the selection). X11 and Wayland (when the compositor lacks `zwp_text_input_v3`) use it: while a text field has the keyboard focus every key goes to the input method first; a consumed key and its key-up never reach the app, the others do, in order. X11 sends the caret in screen pixels (`XTranslateCoordinates`, again when the window moves), Wayland in surface pixels. `xkb.Layout` gained `Keysym` and `XState`.
- **Main files:** `internal/dbus/ime.go`, `internal/dbus/ibus.go`, `internal/dbus/fcitx.go`, `internal/dbus/bus.go` (`ConnectAddress`), `internal/platform/linux/ime/bridge.go`, `internal/platform/linux/ime/imetest/imetest.go`, `internal/platform/linux/x11/textinput.go`, `internal/platform/linux/wayland/dbusime.go`, `internal/platform/linux/xkb/layout.go`
- **Proof:** none (the step has no Proof item).
- **Tests:** against the fake bus, scripted IBus and Fcitx5 sessions (`ime_test.go`): the choice of framework (both running, the hint, only one, neither), the private bus and the portal fallback, every call with its arguments (the `IBusText` signature, the release bit, the X keycode, the capability flags of every purpose), bad replies, and every signal turned into an event (character and byte cursors, hidden preedit, a delete, signals that are ignored); `IBusAddress` for X11, Wayland, remote hosts and the missing cases. On a private `dbus-daemon` (`ime_bus_test.go`): look-alikes of the IBus portal and of Fcitx5 are called and emit the signals with the real wire encoding, and `ConnectAddress`. The bridge (`bridge_test.go`): sending only what changed, the content of every purpose, keys in order, a failing or missing input method, events to `ui.TextInputEvent` (multi-byte text, deletes around the cursor and cut to the text), the reset of a composition, and close with pending keys. X11 (`textinput_test.go`): keys go straight to the app without a field, the field waits for the keyboard focus, consumed keys and their key-ups are dropped, the keysym and modifiers, repeats, events, another window, the window closing, the caret following the window. Wayland (`dbusime_test.go`, fake compositor): used only without the manager, the focus, consumed keys, repeats through the input method, events. Every new tag has a route test: `InputMethodUnavailable`, `InputMethodBadReply`, `IBusAddressNotFound`, `DBusAddressDialFailed`.

- **Main files:** `ui/clipboard.go`, `ui/platform_dispatcher.go`, `services/clipboard.go`, `internal/platform/clipboard.go`, `internal/platform/fake/fake.go`, `internal/renderhost/renderhost.go`, `internal/engine/engine.go`, `internal/platform/linux/wayland/clipboard.go`, `internal/platform/linux/wayland/fakecomp/selection.go`, `internal/platform/linux/x11/clipboard.go`, `widgets/editable_text_state.go`, `widgets/text_selection_gesture.go`, `widgets/selectable_region.go`, `gluttertest/tester.go`
- **Proof:** none (the step has no Proof item).
- **Tests:** fake-platform tests (`internal/platform/linux/wayland/clipboard_rich_test.go`, against the fake compositor): reading images, files and text of another app's selection, a format the owner lacks, setting every format and reading each from the compositor's side, offering only the formats the content has, the primary selection (read, clear, set, loss to another app, replacing its source, a compositor without the manager), and the URI list helpers. Display tests (`internal/platform/linux/x11/clipboard_rich_test.go`, run with `scripts/headless-x11.sh`): the primary selection and the clipboard between two clients, images and files, a format the owner lacks, a 1.6 MB image through `INCR`, an owner that reads its own content. The `INCR` tests exposed a lost wakeup of the X11 event loop (about 5% of runs): Xlib can read events while a flush waits to write a large request, and the loop then slept with them in its queue. `connSource.BeforeWait` now flushes first and handles events until a flush brings none (0 failures in 80 runs). `TestDisplayEGLContextDrawsPurple` fails sometimes under Xvfb (software EGL has no visual); it does not touch the clipboard. `ui` (the host, its fallback to the text host, `ClipboardUnavailable`), the engine with the fake platform, and the widgets with `gluttertest`: selecting text in a field and a drag set the primary selection once per frame, a caret does not, nothing on macOS, obscured text never, a middle click pastes at the pointer (not on Windows, not in a read-only field, nothing when the primary selection is empty), `SelectableRegion` sets it when the selection is final, and the clipboard holds images and files. `ClipboardPrimaryUnavailable` has a route test. The display test of the step, text between two windows of one process, is the X11 one (two clients in one process); there is none for Wayland, as the compositor is a fake.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go test -tags glutter_display ./internal/platform/linux/x11` under `scripts/headless-x11.sh` ✅ · `go test -tags glutter_release` and `-tags glutter_profile` on `./widgets ./services ./ui ./gluttertest ./internal/engine` ✅

Not done: pasting images and files into a widget (the API reads them; `EditableText` pastes text only), clearing the primary selection when a selection is cleared (as GTK does not), `MULTIPLE` and `TIMESTAMP` targets on X11, and drag and drop (step 14.6).

## 11.7 `examples/editor`

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-11.7-editor-example
- **Summary:** `examples/editor`, a text editor on a `WidgetsApp` without Material, with public packages only. A multi-line `EditableText` (the mouse through a `TextSelectionGestureDetectorBuilder`, as `TextField` does: caret, word, line, drag, middle-click paste) with undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Shift+Ctrl+Z from the default text shortcuts, and Ctrl+Y added in a `Shortcuts`), a `Shortcuts` binding of Ctrl+S to a `saveIntent` that writes `$XDG_DATA_HOME/glutter-editor/notes.txt` (`~/.local/share/...` without it) through a temporary file, in a goroutine of `State.Go` with its `context.Context`, and a read-only `SelectableRegion` panel with the saved file. The status bar shows the line and column of the caret, the lines, words and characters, the selected characters, and the state (Loaded, Modified, Saving, Saved with the path, or the error of a failed load or save, in red). The saved file is loaded into the editor at start. In debug builds `GLUTTER_DEV_DATA_DIR`, `GLUTTER_DEV_TEXT` and `GLUTTER_DEV_SELECT` set the directory, the text and the selection, for the proof image.
- **Bug found by the proof image and fixed:** `ParagraphLayout.GetBoxesForRange` with `BoxWidthStyle.max` (the default of `EditableText` on native platforms) extended every box to the widest line, so a selected word in a multi-line field was painted as a full-width bar. It now extends a line only where the selection goes past its edge (SPEC §12.10, the `getBoxesForRange` row): at the start when the range holds the first character of the line, at the end when it holds the line break or goes on to the next line. A word in the middle of a line and the last line of the text stay tight, as in Flutter's `paragraph_test.dart` ('fifth' is not extended). `TestBoxWidthStyleMax` covers it.
- **Main files:** `examples/editor/main.go`, `examples/editor/editor_test.go`, `internal/text/layout/boxes.go`
- **Proof:** `docs/implemented-proof-images/11.7-editor.png` (checked by looking at it): the text with a selection over two lines (block shaped, tight at both ends), the saved copy that is older than the text, and the status bar with `Ln 5, Col 12 (23 selected)`, the counts and `Modified`. The caret is not in the image: a field with a range selected has no caret (Flutter paints it only for a collapsed selection), and its place is the extent of the selection, which the status bar names.
- **Tests:** `gluttertest`: type (the status bar counts it), select a word with a double click, replace it, undo (Ctrl+Z), redo (Shift+Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y), save with Ctrl+S into a temporary directory (the file, the path in the status bar, the panel shows the text, the next key says Modified); the saved file is loaded at start and the panel can select all and copy to the clipboard; a failed save shows the error in the status bar and keeps the text; no data directory shows its error and Ctrl+S does nothing. Functions: the data directory (`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `HOME`, none), save and load, the counts (columns and selections count characters, not bytes), the options of the environment. Every failure has its own route test: `EditorNoDataDir`, `EditorLoadCanceled`, `EditorReadFailed`, `EditorSaveCanceled`, `EditorCreateDirFailed`, `EditorWriteFailed`, `EditorRenameFailed` (and that the temporary file goes away), `EditorSelectInvalid`. One golden image (`examples/editor/testdata/goldens/editor.png`, the same scene as the proof).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go test -tags glutter_release` and `-tags glutter_profile` on `./examples/editor ./internal/text/... ./rendering ./widgets` ✅
- **Manual checks (for the user, not done):** type with IBus or Fcitx5 (for example Pinyin or Japanese) into `go run ./examples/editor` on Wayland (`GLUTTER_BACKEND=wayland`) and on X11 (`GLUTTER_BACKEND=x11`), and confirm that the preedit is underlined while composing and that the commit puts the text in. Also: select text in the editor with the mouse and middle-click in the panel's window or another app, right-click is not wired (the context menu needs Material, step 13). The answer is not recorded here: the session had no way to ask; nothing about typing with a real input method has been verified yet (the tests play the input method through `SendTextInputEvent` and the D-Bus fakes of steps 11.2 and 11.3).
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the example has no context menu or selection handles (`SelectionControls` are the empty ones, as on desktop); the text is Roboto, as the only bundled font has no monospaced face. In SPEC §12.10 the `getBoxesForRange` row was updated for the width style.

- **Date:** 2026-10-20

- **Summary:** `examples/counter` is the reference example of SPEC §12.12 on package `material` alone: a Material 3 app with an app bar titled "Counter", the text and the number, and a floating action button with a "+" that adds one. For it, the minimum of three Material widgets exists: `Scaffold` (app bar, body and floating action button slots, laid out as Flutter's `_ScaffoldLayout` does, with the button at the end of the bottom, `endFloat`), `AppBar` (surface color, a 64 px toolbar, the title large style, 16 px of spacing, the leading and actions slots, the safe area on top) and `FloatingActionButton` (the regular 56 px button: 16 px radius, primary container colors, elevation 6, ink, 24 px icon, the tooltip as the semantics tooltip). The widgets layer got `NavigationToolbar` (a full port) and the `PreferredSizeWidget` interface.
- **Main files:** `examples/counter/main.go`, `material/scaffold.go`, `app_bar.go`, `floating_action_button.go`, `widgets/navigation_toolbar.go`, `preferred_size.go`, `material/fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf`, `scripts/fetch-fonts.sh`
- **Proof:** `docs/implemented-proof-images/12.5-counter.png` (method B, the real app on the GLES renderer under headless sway with `GLUTTER_DEV_TAPS=3`; checked by looking at it): the title "Counter", the text "You have pushed the button this many times:", the number 3 and the blue floating action button with a "+".

Flutter has no test file for `NavigationToolbar`, and the tests of `Scaffold`, `AppBar` and the button come with 13.1 and 13.3.

The widgets are marked `TODO(step 13.1)` and `TODO(step 13.3)`. **A defect of earlier steps was found and fixed:** the bundled Material Icons font came from Google's `material-design-icons` repository, whose code points are not Flutter's (`Icons.add` is `0xe047` in Flutter, `0xe145` there), so every generated icon drew another glyph (`add` was a filled square). The font is now the `MaterialIcons-Regular.otf` of the archive that the Flutter SDK downloads (named in `bin/internal/material_fonts.version` of the pinned Flutter commit); `scripts/fetch-fonts.sh`, `material/fonts/VERSIONS`, `NOTICE` and the SPEC (§10, §20) follow it, the tests that used `0xe145` use `0xe047`, and `TestIconsRenderFromTheBundledFont` now tells a plus from a square. **License to check:** the license text that ships with that font in Flutter's archive is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (the old file was Apache-2.0); it is bundled as `MaterialIcons-LICENSE.txt` and named in `NOTICE`.

## 14.1 Window decorations

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.1-window-decorations
- **Summary:** a Wayland window is decorated by the first of these that works (SPEC §8.2): the compositor (`zxdg_decoration_manager_v1`), libdecor (a new binding of `libdecor-0.so.0` through purego, with its file descriptor in the event loop), and Glutter's `WindowDecoration` widget (title, minimize, maximize or restore and close buttons limited by `wm_capabilities`, a drag of the bar to move, a double tap to maximize or restore, a right click for the window menu, and edge and corner resizing). `WindowConfig.Decorations` (`DecorationsAuto`, `DecorationsApp`) and `GLUTTER_DECORATIONS=auto|app|libdecor` choose; the platform reports the mode, the title, the capabilities and the state of the window in `ViewMetrics.Window`, which the framework reads with `View.Window()`, and the title bar of the app asks for moves and resizes with `View.PerformWindowAction`. `RunApp` shows a `WindowDecoration` when the window needs one.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/linux/wayland/decor/` (the libdecor binding), `internal/platform/linux/wayland/decoration.go`, `window.go`, `platform.go`, `pointer.go`, `fakecomp/windowing.go`; `internal/platform/window.go`, `platform.go`, `fake/`, `linux/x11/window.go`; `internal/engine/engine.go`; `ui/window_info.go`, `view.go`, `platform_dispatcher.go`; `widgets/window_decoration.go`, `run_app.go`; `gluttertest/tester.go` (`WindowActions`), `internal/renderhost`; `material/widgets_reexport_gen.go` (generated).
- **Tests:** `decor` (the layouts of the two interface structs, the routes of `LibdecorInitFailed`, `LibdecorDecorateFailed` and `LibdecorDispatchFailed` through functions that fail), `wayland/decoration_test` (the mode for each compositor and config, the state and the capabilities reported, every action of the title bar as an `xdg_toplevel` request, and the close), `engine` (the info and the actions both ways, `GLUTTER_DECORATIONS` and the route of `DecorationsUnknown`), `widgets/window_decoration_test` (the bar only when the app draws it, each button and the capabilities that limit them, the drag, the double tap and the right click, the eight resize handles and none when maximized, fullscreen or tiled, the state of the child kept when the bar appears, the options). Display tests under sway: the mode follows the compositor, and a libdecor window answers its configure and maps. The existing tests of the Wayland platform and the scale tests ignore `ViewMetrics.Window`.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · display tests (`-tags glutter_display`, the two new ones, under sway) ✅
- **Measurements (item 4), the counter example on the GNOME 50 session of this machine, the window open for two seconds, three runs each:**

  | | first window (from the connection to "renderer ready") | peak RSS |
  |---|---|---|
  | `GLUTTER_DECORATIONS=app` (no libdecor) | 0.0 s | 212 MB |
  | libdecor with the GTK plugin | 2.1 s | 236–241 MB |
  | libdecor with the cairo plugin only (`LIBDECOR_PLUGIN_DIR`) | 0.0 s | 218 MB |

  So the GTK plugin (GTK 3 in the process) costs about two seconds and 25 MB; the cairo plugin costs 5 MB and no time, but draws its own look, not Adwaita. The GTK plugin is the one that matches Flutter on GNOME, so it stays the default; a program that does not want it sets `DecorationsApp` or `LIBDECOR_PLUGIN_DIR`.

## 14.2 Multiple windows

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.2-multiple-windows
- **Summary:** an app can show several windows: `RegularWindowController` with `RegularWindow`, and `DialogWindowController` with `DialogWindow` (modal to its parent: `xdg_toplevel.set_parent` and `xdg_dialog_v1.set_modal` on Wayland, `WM_TRANSIENT_FOR` and `_NET_WM_STATE_MODAL` on X11, and closed with the parent), in a `ViewCollection`, a `ViewAnchor`, or a `WindowManager` with its `WindowRegistry`. `WindowScope` gives a window's widgets its controller and state, and the first window has a controller too. The names are those of the pinned Flutter (`widgets/_window.dart`); SPEC §8.7 said `WindowController` and `Window`. The engine draws every window with one `gles.Renderer`, one GL context and a surface for each, runs one framework frame for the windows that asked for one, and routes the cursor, the input method and the view focus events to the window they belong to. `View` follows the view focus events (`DidChangeViewFocus`, `RequestViewFocusChange`), so the focus and the keyboard follow the active window.
- **Main files:** `widgets/view_collection.go` (`ViewCollection`, `ViewAnchor`), `window_controller.go` (the controllers, the delegates, `WindowingOwner`), `window_scope.go` (`WindowScope`, `RegularWindow`, `DialogWindow`), `window_manager.go`, `view.go` (the focus events), `binding.go`, `run_app.go`; `ui/window_control.go` (`WindowSpec`, `WindowControlHost`, the view focus types), `platform_dispatcher.go`, `view.go`, `window_info.go`; `internal/engine/engine.go` (the windows, the shared renderer); `internal/platform/` (`Handler.OnViewFocus`, `Window.SetSizeConstraints`), `fake/`, `linux/wayland/` (`xdg_dialog_v1`, size limits, view focus from the keyboard, the actions), `linux/x11/` (the actions, `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW`, size hints, view focus), `fakecomp/windowing.go`; `gluttertest/windows.go`, `gestures.go` (`GestureOpts.View`), `internal/renderhost`; `examples/multiwindow`; `material/widgets_reexport_gen.go` (generated).
- **Tests:** 62 new Go test functions (many with subtests). `widgets`: the controllers, the delegates, the scope and its aspects, the registry and the manager, the focus between windows (`window_controller_test.go`); the cases of Flutter below (`view_collection_test.go`). `engine/windows_test.go` (13): the windows of the framework as platform configs (kind, parent, modal, app ID, decorations, not resizable), a platform failure, title, size and limits, destroy and the surface released, one presented frame for each frame request (and the window that asked for none is not drawn), a frame that renders nothing, a window with no size, the close request (taken by the window owner, cancelled by the app, or agreed), closing the first window, view focus and input, the activation a focus request makes, the actions of each window, and input for a window that has a scene waiting. `wayland/windows_test.go` (5): dialogs against the fake compositor (with and without `xdg_wm_dialog_v1`, modal or not, with or without a parent, and the order of the destroys), size limits, a window that cannot be resized, the keyboard focus as a view focus, the new actions. `fake`: the limits and the focus event. `examples/multiwindow` (5). **Display tests (`-tags glutter_display`, under sway): `TestDisplayThreeWindowsAndADialog`**: two windows and a modal dialog of the first one are configured and mapped, sway has all three, and they close one at a time, the parent first, until Run returns. **Ported from Flutter: 13 cases of `view_test.dart`** (in 10 Go tests) (ViewCollection may start with zero views; ViewAnchor.child does not see the surrounding view; ViewAnchor layout order; visitChildren of ViewAnchor and of ViewCollection; the three of the render object getter; the four of the view focus: unfocusing and refocusing, the notification of the engine, switching focus between views, a nested view and the surrounding view) **and 30 cases of `windowing_test.dart`** (a RegularWindow and a DialogWindow do not throw; `WindowScope.of`, `maybeOf` and the six getters with their `maybe` forms, each for the regular and the dialog window). Not ported: the cases for tooltips, popups and satellites (deferred), the group where windowing is off (it is always on), 'cannot have multiple views with same FlutterView' (the key of the view is an `ObjectKey`, SPEC §12.10), the `View` cases about the deprecated pipeline owner and render view, and the `multi_view_*` tests, which need the `FlutterView` test doubles of flutter_test.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · display tests (`-tags glutter_display`, the wayland package under sway) ✅ · `go test -tags glutter_release` and `-tags glutter_profile` ✅

  ![14.2 three windows](implemented-proof-images/14.2-multiwindow.png)
  Method C, `GLUTTER_DEV_OPEN=window,dialog go run ./examples/multiwindow` on the GLES renderer under headless sway (`scripts/headless-wayland.sh`), the windows then placed with `swaymsg` and captured with grim: the main window, a second window ("Window 1", each with the counter and its three buttons, drawn through the one shared GL context) and the dialog ("Dialog"), floating over the main window. sway draws the title bars. sway has no `xdg_wm_dialog_v1` and shows no sign of the parent of a dialog (it centers every floating window), so the relation itself is checked against the fake compositor.

Input could not be sent to the windows of a real compositor: the headless sway has no input device (the seat has no capabilities, so `swaymsg seat ... cursor press` reaches nobody). Input to the other windows is tested with the fake engine (events with the view of the window) and the engine tests; clicking in the second window and the dialog under a desktop compositor is not yet seen.

## 14.3 Outputs and scaling

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.3-outputs-and-scaling
- **Summary:** the platforms know their monitors. On Wayland every `wl_output` (up to v4, also one plugged in later, and gone on `wl_registry.global_remove`) is kept with its mode, scale, transform and name, and `zxdg_output_manager_v1` adds the logical position and size, so `Displays()` lists the outputs with bounds in logical pixels, an exact pixel ratio (a 150% output says 1.5), the refresh rate in Hz and the primary one. A window's metrics name its display (the entered output with the largest scale), and a window that moves to an output of another scale is resized, reported and drawn at once at the new scale (the machinery of 3.7/11.x already sizes the buffer, the viewport and the first commit). The engine hands the dispatcher the new display list whenever it changes (`OnDisplaysChanged`) and gives the views their display again. On X11, `Displays()` comes from `XRRGetMonitors`, the scale is `Xft.dpi` ÷ 96 (read from `RESOURCE_MANAGER`, and followed live) or, without it, the monitor's own density when it is 144 dpi or more; a window is made in logical pixels × its monitor's scale, and follows `RRScreenChangeNotify`, `Xft.dpi` changes and the moves between monitors.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/linux/wayland/outputs.go` (the outputs, `Displays`, `displayOf`), `conn.go` (binding and hotplug), `window.go` (`ViewMetrics.Display`, `displayChanged`), `platform.go`; `internal/platform/linux/x11/monitors.go` (monitors, `Xft.dpi`, scale, `Displays`), `lib.go`/`structs.go` (the XRandR functions, `XRRMonitorInfo`), `window.go` (scaled sizes, `updateScale`), `events.go`, `textinput.go` (caret in device pixels); `internal/platform/platform.go` (`Handler.OnDisplaysChanged`), `nop.go`, `fake/events.go` (`DisplaysEvent`); `internal/engine/engine.go`; `scripts/headless-wayland.sh` (`HEADLESS_SECOND`); the fake compositor (`fakecomp`) with outputs that come and go, a mode, names, `zxdg_output_v1`, and per-output scale, enter and leave.
- **Tests:** Wayland on the fake compositor: `TestDisplaysDescribeTheOutputs` (wl_output only, a logical size that gives 2.5, a transform of 90 degrees), `TestOutputsComeAndGo` (plug in, unplug, release), `TestTheViewMetricsNameTheDisplayOfTheWindow` (the display follows enter/leave, the scale follows the output, a frame at the new size). Engine: `TestDisplayChangesReachTheDispatcherAndTheViews`. Fake platform: the `DisplaysEvent` case. X11: `TestParseXftDPI`, `TestScaleFor`, `TestMonitorAtFallsBackToThePrimaryMonitor`, the `XRRMonitorInfo` layout. Display tests: Wayland `TestDisplayMovingBetweenOutputsRescalesTheNextFrame` (sway headless with two outputs, `HEADLESS_SECOND=800x600@2 scripts/headless-wayland.sh`: `Displays()` has both, the window moved with `swaymsg` to the scale-2 output and back, the metrics follow at once and the next buffer committed has the size of the new scale), X11 `TestDisplayXftDPIScalesTheWindowAndFollowsChanges` and `TestDisplayWindowIsMadeInLogicalPixels` (an `Xft.dpi` written to the root window from another connection). Two tests of 14.2 that read the requests of the fake compositor before it had them (`TestSizeConstraints`, `TestDialogs`) failed about one run in four under load; they now wait.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · display tests (`-tags glutter_display`: wayland under sway with and without `HEADLESS_SECOND`, with `HEADLESS_SCALE=1.5`, x11 under Xvfb) ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅
- **Proof:** none listed for this step; the display test above is the proof.
- **Manual checks:** none. Real mixed-DPI desktops (GNOME or KDE with a 100% and a 200% monitor) are not tried yet.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** 3 new rows in SPEC §12.10 (`Display`, the display in the metrics, the scale of X11 windows) and §8.2, §8.3 and §8.11 updated. Not done: XSETTINGS on X11 (`Gdk/WindowScalingFactor`, `Xft/DPI`; the settings of 14.5 bring them), a window that keeps its logical size when it moves between X11 monitors, and the refresh rate of each X11 monitor (all have the screen's rate; XRandR reports it per CRTC).

## 14.4 Cursors, complete

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.4-cursors
- **Summary:** every `SystemMouseCursors` value reaches the platform as a `wp_cursor_shape_v1` shape and as XCursor names (CSS name first, then the older X names), and the XCursor path now follows the settings and the scale. Wayland without cursor shapes: the theme and size are the settings' (else `XCURSOR_THEME`/`XCURSOR_SIZE`, else 24), loaded for each integer scale in use at the size × scale; the cursor surface gets that buffer scale and the hotspot is divided by it; the cursor is set again when the window's scale or the settings change. X11: the theme and size go to libXcursor (`XcursorSetTheme`, `XcursorSetDefaultSize`) with the size × the scale of the window's monitor, a cursor is loaded once per size, and set again when the scale or the settings change. `cursors.configure(theme, size)` of both backends is what the settings of 14.5 will call.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/linux/wayland/cursor.go` (themes per scale, `configure`, `scaleChanged`), `window.go`; `internal/platform/linux/x11/cursor.go` (sizes, theme, `configure`), `lib.go` (`XcursorSetTheme`, `XcursorSetDefaultSize`), `monitors.go` (cursor again on a new scale).
- **Tests:** `TestEveryCursorHasItsNames` (all 36 cursors: the CSS name first and the old X name, no duplicates, none left out) and `TestEveryCursorHasItsShape` (all 36: the `wp_cursor_shape_v1` value, none left out); Wayland `TestCursorFromTheThemeIsLoadedAtTheScaleOfTheWindow` (theme at 48 with buffer scale 2 and the hotspot halved, then at 24 when the scale goes to 1) and `TestCursorThemeAndSizeFromTheSettings` (settings over the environment, the same settings change nothing, empty settings go back); X11 `TestCursorSizeAndThemeFollowTheSettingsAndTheScale` (7 cases) and `TestCursorsAreLoadedAgainForAnotherScaleOrSettings`; display test `TestDisplayCursorsHaveTheSizeOfTheScale` (Xvfb, `Xft.dpi` 192 gives a cursor of 48).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests (wayland under sway, x11 under Xvfb) ✅
- **Proof:** none listed for this step.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** 1 new row in SPEC §12.10 (the cursor names: the GTK embedder's own table is not in `reference/`, so the lists come from the CSS names and the names of Adwaita, Breeze and the X11 fonts), §8.3 and §8.11 updated. Not done: animated cursors (the first image is used), and reading the theme and size from the settings, which comes with 14.5. A cursor that the theme has under none of its names still leaves the previous one in place (logged once).

## 14.5 Live system settings

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.5-live-settings
- **Summary:** the Wayland and X11 platforms now read the system settings and follow them while the app runs. `linux.SettingsWatcher` connects to the session bus (only when one is there, so nothing starts `dbus-launch`), reads the Settings portal and follows `SettingChanged`; each change is posted to the UI thread, sets the cursor theme and size (`cursors.configure`, 14.4) and reaches the engine as `Handler.OnSettings`, which updates the dispatcher, so `MediaQuery` (`PlatformBrightness`, text scale, `DisableAnimations`) and `ThemeMode.system` change at once. The locale comes from `LC_ALL`/`LC_MESSAGES`/`LANG` (`dbus.LocalesFromEnv`). On X11 without the portal the XSETTINGS daemon is followed (`_XSETTINGS_S<screen>`, its property, `MANAGER` messages for a new daemon): a dark theme, the cursor theme and size, animations, font smoothing and hinting, and `Gdk/WindowScalingFactor` as the monitors' scale when there is no `Xft.dpi`.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/linux/settings.go` (`SettingsWatcher`), `internal/dbus/settings.go` (`LocalesFromEnv`, `WatchPortalSettings`), `internal/platform/linux/wayland/platform.go` and `x11/platform.go` (`Settings`, `applySettings`), `x11/xsettings.go`, `x11/events.go`, `x11/monitors.go`; `internal/engine/engine.go` (`PlatformConfiguration` exported for the tests of the layers above).
- **Tests:** `dbus`: `TestLocalesFromEnv` (12 cases), `TestWatchPortalSettingsSaysWhereTheSettingsCameFrom`, the fallback with a locale. `linux`: `TestSettingsWatcherFollowsThePortal`, `…WithoutAPortal`, `…SetAndReplace`, `TestSessionBusPresent`. Wayland on the fake compositor with a fake bus: `TestSettingsComeFromThePortalAndFollowItsChanges` (the portal's values, the locale, a scheme change, the cursor size and the text scale reach `OnSettings` and the cursors, an unchanged value is not passed on) and `TestSettingsWithoutAPortalComeFromTheEnvironment`. X11: `TestParseXSettings` (both byte orders, colors, padding), `TestParseXSettingsToleratesBadData` (every cut of the data), `TestApplyXSettings` (13 cases), `TestXSettingsScale`, and the display test `TestDisplaySettingsFromXSettingsFollowTheDaemon` (a settings daemon of the test on Xvfb: dark theme and cursor at the start, a light theme and animations off while running). `widgets`: `TestASettingsSignalChangesTheMediaQuery`: a signal on a fake bus changes `MediaQuery.PlatformBrightness`, the text scale and `DisableAnimations`, through the watcher, `engine.PlatformConfiguration` and the dispatcher, the app rebuilding for each. The engine's `TestPortalSettingsReachTheDispatcher` already covered the dispatcher.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · display tests (wayland under sway, x11 under Xvfb) ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅ · the gallery starts under sway and takes its screenshot with the new settings path

## 14.6 Drag and drop with other apps

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.6-drag-and-drop
- **Summary:** `Draggable`, `LongPressDraggable` and `DragTarget` are ported from `widgets/drag_target.dart` (with the `MetaData` widget they need), and the platforms take part in drag and drop. *In the window:* the avatar, the hit test for the targets, the entered and active targets, the axes, `maxSimultaneousDrags`, the recognizer that outlives a removed `Draggable`. *Between applications:* the windows are drop targets (Wayland `wl_data_device` `enter`/`motion`/`leave`/`drop`, with accept, the actions and `finish`; X11 XDND v5 with `XdndAware`, the position and status messages, `XdndSelection` and `XdndFinished`) and the platform reads the text and the URIs of a drop; a `Draggable` with `Export` starts a drag of the platform (Wayland `start_drag` with a data source and an icon surface; X11 the XDND source that follows the pointer from the XInput2 events). A `DragTarget` receives the drags of other applications as `*ExternalDragData` (`Types` during the drag; `Text`, `URIs`, `Files()` after the drop); the drags of the app that come back to it carry the `Draggable`'s own data, found by a marker type `application/x-glutter-drag-<pid>-<id>`. `examples/multiwindow` has "Drag me" and a drop zone that shows the paths of the files dropped on it.
- **Main files:** `widgets/drag_target.go` (the port), `drag_drop.go` (the bridge: external avatars, `Export`, `handleDrop`), `meta_data.go`; `ui/drag_drop.go` (`DropEvent`, `DropActions`, `DragRequest`, `DragResult`, `DropHost`, the dispatcher's `OnDrop`, `OnDragEnd`, `StartDrag`); `internal/platform` (`Handler.OnDrop` returns the action, `OnDragEnd`, `Window.StartDrag(ui.DragRequest)`); `internal/engine/engine.go`; `internal/platform/linux/wayland/dnd.go`, `dndicon.go`, `clipboard.go`, `shm.go`; `internal/platform/linux/x11/dnd.go`, `input.go`, `events.go`; the fake compositor (`fakecomp/dnd.go`); `gluttertest` (`Tester.Drop`, `Drags`, `FailDrags`); `examples/multiwindow`.
- **Tests:** 31 cases ported from `draggable_test.dart` in `widgets/drag_target_test.go` (the control test, `onLeave`, `onMove`, null data, long press with the default and custom delays, the three axes and `onDragUpdate` along an axis, the end callbacks for accepting, refusing and no target, pass-through of unaccepted data, the builder's candidate and rejected data, `DragTarget<Object>` taking an int, another type not seeing it, `maxSimultaneousDrags`, `childWhenDragging`, removing the draggable in the middle of a drag, `onTap`, the three anchor strategies, `allowedButtonsFilter`, the hit test behavior, the negative `maxSimultaneousDrags`); not ported: semantics, Ahem-metric text positions, scaled and rotated apps, the cursor test, the root overlay tests, the deprecated callbacks. The bridge: `widgets/drag_drop_test.go` (8: an external drag over a target, enter, move, leave and drop with the data and `Files()`; targets of another type; refusing by type; a drop where nothing accepts; `Export` starting a platform drag, local data, the end; the fallback in the window; no data) and the example's two tests. Wayland on the fake compositor (`dnd_test.go`, 8: enter, move and leave with the position, types and actions; accept and `set_actions`; a refused drag; a drop with the data and `finish`; a drop answered with none; the local marker; the app's own drag, its data read by the target, the action and the end, and a cancel; no button, no data device, a pipe that cannot be made); X11 on Xvfb (`TestDisplayDragBetweenTwoWindows`: a drag from one window to another over the real XDND messages and selection, the data and the result; `TestDisplayDragNobodyTakes`; a closed window); `ui` and engine tests of the new API.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable (the `material` re-exports have the new widgets) ✅ · display tests (wayland under sway, x11 under Xvfb) ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅

Not done from here: the headless sway has no pointer, so no drag can start or arrive on a real Wayland compositor (the X11 test covers the same code path for XDND with a real server). ## 14.7 The remaining Wayland quality items

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.7-wayland-quality
- **Summary:** the optional Wayland protocols of SPEC §8.11 are used. *Activation:* `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` is read at startup, removed from the environment, and used once for the first window (`xdg_activation_v1.activate`); `activate()` on a window controller and a focus request ask for a token (with the serial of the last input event, the app id and the surface) and activate the window with it; `Platform.RequestActivationToken` (the optional interface `platform.ActivationTokenProvider`) gives a token for an app this app starts, which M15 uses. *Idle inhibit:* `desktop.KeepScreenOn(bc, on) error` (and `ui.View.KeepScreenOn`) makes or destroys a `zwp_idle_inhibitor_v1` for the window, and fails with `IdleInhibitUnavailable` without the protocol (also on X11, for now). *Tablets:* `zwp_tablet_manager_v2` tools become stylus, inverted stylus, touch or mouse pointer devices (`input.StylusBatcher`: Add, Hover, Down, Move, Up, Remove from the events between two `frame`s, pressure, distance, tilt and azimuth, the barrel buttons; the cursor by shape). *Content type:* `WindowConfig.ContentType` and `SetContentType` through `wp_content_type_v1`. *Window icon:* `WindowConfig.Icon` and `SetIcon` through `xdg_toplevel_icon_v1` (a theme name and square RGBA pictures as `wl_shm` buffers). Both windows controllers take `Icon` and `ContentType` and have `SetIcon` and `SetContentType`. `scripts/wayland-matrix.sh` runs the display tests and every example under sway, weston, `mutter --headless` and `kwin_wayland --virtual`, and `docs/wayland-checklist.md` is the manual part for the user.
- **Fixed on the way:** (1) the positions of the pointer and of the touch points on Wayland were not multiplied by the window's scale (the batchers' `Scale` was never set), so a click at 200% landed at half the position; the pointer, the touch points and the tablet tools now use `scale/120`, with a test at scale 2. (2) `internal/dbus` `forward` panicked with a nil pointer when the connection closed while a subscription was live (godbus closes the signal channels); found by the matrix under mutter (`animations` exited with status 2) and covered by `TestRealBusCloseWhileSubscribed`. (3) The GPU parity display tests: `decorations` and `rendering-tour` had no tolerance (the failure that was open since 14.1: 1.0 and 0.1 permille over 8 levels, the edges of rounded corners and shadows), the nearest-neighbor image of "color filters and inverted colors" had a pixel center exactly on a texel edge (the GPU of mutter and kwin rounds the other way: the source is now 31 texels wide), and the mask filters scene gets a tolerance of one pixel (9 levels off on kwin's GPU). (4) The physics tests that expect a debug-only panic ran under `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` and failed; they skip there.

## 14.8 X11 parity

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-14.8-x11-parity
- **Summary:** the X11 backend reaches the level of the Wayland one for what the window manager does. *Window state:* the backend follows `_NET_WM_STATE` (maximized needs both axes, fullscreen), `WM_STATE` and `_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN` (minimized), `_NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS` (the capabilities; a manager that lists none allows all) and the keyboard focus (activated), and the app hears of a change as new `ViewMetrics.Window` (`WindowInfo.Minimized` is new, and `IsMinimized` of the window controllers uses it where the platform says). *`_NET_WM_ICON`:* `WindowConfig.Icon` and `SetIcon` (the pictures as ARGB; the theme name has no X11 counterpart; an empty icon removes the property). *`_MOTIF_WM_HINTS` for `DecorationsApp`:* the window manager is told to draw no decorations, the window says `DecorationApp`, so `WindowDecoration` draws the title bar, and its moves, edge resizes and window menu go to the window manager as `_NET_WM_MOVERESIZE` and `_GTK_SHOW_WINDOW_MENU` (after `XIUngrabDevice` ends the grab of the press). *XRandR hot-plug:* the backend also selects the output and CRTC events (`RRNotify`), and the handler is told once when the monitors or the scale changed. XI2 touch, `INCR` selections and XDND were already there (steps 11 and 14.6); this step checks them again under Xvfb.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/linux/x11/wmstate.go` (state, icon, move, resize, menu, `info`), `window.go`, `input.go` (the last press, the focus), `events.go`, `monitors.go`, `platform.go` (atoms), `lib.go` (`XIUngrabDevice`); `ui/window_info.go` (`Minimized`); `widgets/window_controller.go`; tests `wm_display_test.go` (a small EWMH window manager on its own connection), `hotplug_display_test.go`, `display_test.go`.
- **Tests (display, under Xvfb):** `wm_display_test.go`, with `testWM`, a window manager of the test (it redirects the map and configure requests of the root, keeps `_NET_WM_STATE` and `WM_STATE`, resizes for maximized and fullscreen, iconifies, focuses, and records the moves and menus): `TestDisplayWindowStatesFollowTheWindowManager` (maximize, fullscreen, normal, minimize, restore, and the title bar's own actions, with the sizes the manager gives), `TestDisplayAllowedActionsLimitTheCapabilities` and `TestDisplayWithoutAListOfAllowedActionsEveryOneIsAllowed`, `TestDisplayActivatedFollowsTheFocus` (the focus from the manager and the activation request), `TestDisplayWindowIconIsNetWMIcon` (the data of the property for one and two pictures, a wrong picture, the empty icon, a window with a wrong icon), `TestDisplayDecorationsOfTheApp` (4 cases: the Motif hints and the decoration mode for a decorated, an app-drawn, an undecorated and a borderless window), `TestDisplayMoveResizeAndMenuGoToTheWindowManager` (the move, the eight directions, the menu at the right root position, nothing without a button), `TestDisplayTheServerTakesTouchAndTheWindowSelectsIt` (XInput 2.2 and no X error from selecting touch). `hotplug_display_test.go`: `TestDisplayMonitorsComeAndGo` (a real monitor added and removed on the server with `XRRSetMonitor`; the events that Xvfb does not send, because it has one output, are handed to the event handler: `Displays()` has the new monitor with its bounds, one notification, none for events that change no monitor, one when it goes away). Unit: `widgets` `TestAPlatformThatSaysWhenAWindowIsMinimizedIsBelieved`, `x11` the stubs of 14.7 (`TestKeepScreenOnIsUnavailableOnX11`). The tests that were there stay: the touch events (unit), `INCR` for text and images (`TestClipboardLargeTextUsesIncrementalTransfer`, `TestClipboardLargeImageUsesIncrementalTransfer`) and the drag between two windows over XDND (`TestDisplayDragBetweenTwoWindows`) run under Xvfb too.

## 15.1 Portal plumbing and OpenURI

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.1-portal-open-uri
- **Summary:** package `desktop` gets its plumbing and its first service. *The parent of a dialog:* a window can say how the portals name it: Wayland exports it with `zxdg_exporter_v2.export_toplevel` once, keeps the `wayland:<handle>` until the window closes, and answers every waiting caller; X11 says `x11:<window id in hex>`; a compositor without the exporter gives an empty handle. It reaches the framework through `ui.PortalHost` (`PlatformDispatcher.PortalParentHandle` and `ActivationToken`), which the engine implements with `platform.PortalHandleProvider` (the window) and `platform.ActivationTokenProvider` (14.7). *How a call works:* a call of `desktop` waits for the desktop, so it is made from a goroutine (`DesktopCallOnUIThread` on the UI thread), posts one function to the UI thread for the window handle and the activation token, and does the rest itself; the state (the connection to the session bus) lives in the `WidgetsBinding` (`Extension`). *`desktop.OpenURI(ctx, bc, uri) error`:* the OpenURI portal with the handle, the URI, `handle_token` and `activation_token`, waiting for the `Response` (success and the user's cancel are `nil`); when the portal cannot do it, `xdg-open` with `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN`; then `OpenURIUnavailable`; a URI without a scheme fails with `OpenURIInvalid`.
- **Fixed on the way:** (1) `SetMetadata` of `github.com/rm4n0s/errors` takes all the key/value pairs of the error in one call and a second call *replaces* the first one's, so the chains in `internal/dbus` (`DBusCallFailed`, `DBusSubscribeFailed`), `widgets/localizations.go` and `glutter-gen`'s keys lost all but the last pair; they are single calls now, with a test, and CLAUDE.md says so. (2) The X11 display tests started the event loop on a goroutine that was not locked to its OS thread, so an OpenGL context could be used from another thread than the one that made it current: `TestDisplayEGLContextDrawsPurple` failed about half of the runs alone (`ShaderCompileFailed` or `EGLSwapFailed`) and every test that draws would have, sooner or later. The goroutines of the X11 and `gles` display tests that run the loop lock the thread now, as the main goroutine does in an app (0 failures in 30 runs).
- **Main files:** `desktop/services.go` (the services of the app, `begin`), `open_uri.go`, `screen.go`; `ui/portal.go` (`PortalHost`), `internal/platform/platform.go` (`PortalHandleProvider`), `linux/wayland/extras.go` (the export), `conn.go`, `window.go`, `fakecomp/extras.go` (`zxdg_exporter_v2`), `linux/x11/wmstate.go`; `internal/engine/engine.go`; `widgets/binding.go` (`Extension`); `internal/platform/fake`, `internal/renderhost` (handles and tokens for the tests).
- **Tests:** `desktop/open_uri_test.go` (fake bus with the portal's request and response; the UI thread is the tester's, run by `FlushPosted`): the call and its arguments (handle of the window, URI, activation token), the user who cancels, the four ways to fall back to `xdg-open` (the portal says it ended badly, no portal on the bus, the portal fails the call, no session bus) with the activation token in the environment of the program, `OpenURIUnavailable` with its metadata when `xdg-open` fails too, six invalid URIs that never reach the bus, a context that ends while the user has not answered (`PortalRequestAborted`, the request closed, no `xdg-open`), a call on the UI thread, one without a binding, one that the UI thread never answers (`DesktopCallCancelled`). Wayland on the fake compositor: `TestPortalHandleIsExportedOnceAndKept` (two callers before the handle arrives and one after, one export, destroyed with the window) and `TestPortalHandleWithoutTheExporter`; X11, `fake`, `engine` and `ui`: the handles and the tokens at each layer; `widgets`: `Extension` is made once per binding and key, and is safe from many goroutines. The display test of the optional protocols now also asks for the portal handle (sway, mutter and kwin all give a `wayland:` handle).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · display tests (wayland, gles and engine under sway; x11 and engine under Xvfb, three runs) ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅
- **Proof:** none listed for this step.
- **Manual checks:** **pending, asked of the user:** on a desktop (GNOME or KDE, Wayland and X11), call `desktop.OpenURI` with an `https:` URI from a button of an example (in a goroutine) and see it open in the browser with the app chooser as a child of the window; the same inside a Flatpak, if you use one. The answers are not recorded yet; when they come, update this entry. They do not block the next steps.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** `desktop` has no Flutter counterpart (SPEC §8.9 describes how the calls work). `OpenURI` passes `activation_token` only where the platform gives one (Wayland). Not done: `OpenFile` for a local file with a file descriptor (a `file://` URI goes through `OpenURI`); the Flatpak branch of the notifications came with 15.3.

## 15.2 File dialogs

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.2-file-dialogs
- **Summary:** `desktop.OpenFiles`, `desktop.SaveFile` and `desktop.SaveFiles` open the dialogs of the desktop through `org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser` (`OpenFile`, `SaveFile`, `SaveFiles`), as children of the window of the context (15.1). The options are the portal's: `Title`, `AcceptLabel`, `Filters` (`FileFilter{Name, Patterns, MIMETypes}`, the first is the current one), `Multiple`, `Directory` (no filters then), `CurrentFolder`, `CurrentName` and `CurrentFile` for saving, `NotModal`, and the names for `SaveFiles`. The answer is a `FilesResult{Cancelled, Paths, Filter}`: the `file:` URIs become paths (percent-decoded), a user who closes the dialog gives `Cancelled: true` and no error, and an app that wants the filter the user left selected reads `Filter`. A portal that cannot be reached is `FileChooserUnavailable` (no fallback, as SPEC §8.9 says); the other failures have tags of their own.
- **Main files:** `desktop/file_chooser.go`; tests `desktop/file_chooser_test.go`, `export_test.go`.
- **Tests:** against the fake bus with the portal scripted (`file_chooser_test.go`): `OpenFiles` with everything set (the parent handle and the title, `accept_label`, `multiple`, `modal`, `current_folder` as bytes with a NUL, no `directory`, no activation token, the signature `a(sa(us))` of the filters with the globs before the MIME types and the `(sa(us))` of the current one, the paths decoded, the filter name); directory mode (no filters, `directory` true, `multiple` not set); `SaveFile` (`current_name`, `current_file`, the filter, the method); `SaveFiles` (`aay` of names, the paths); the checks of the names; a cancel as a result for each of the three; `FileChooserUnavailable` for no portal, no bus and no such method (with the method in the metadata); `FileChooserFailed` and three kinds of `FileChooserReplyInvalid`; a context that ends while the dialog is open (the request is closed); a call on the UI thread; two options values panic; `filterName` for the shapes godbus and the test give.

## 15.3 Notifications

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.3-notifications
- **Summary:** `desktop.ShowNotification(ctx, bc, summary, opts) (NotificationID, error)` and `desktop.CloseNotification(ctx, bc, id)` use `org.freedesktop.Notifications` (`Notify`, `CloseNotification`) with the app name, `replaces_id`, icon, body, the actions as ID/label pairs, the hints `urgency`, `desktop-entry` (the app id of the window) and `category`, and the timeout (`Persistent` is 0). The body is escaped where the server has the `body-markup` capability, unless `BodyMarkup` is set. `ActionInvoked` and `NotificationClosed` are followed with one subscription that lives as long as the app and reach `OnAction(actionID)` and `OnClosed(reason)` of the notification on the UI thread (`CallbackPanicked` for a panic); the callbacks of a notification are dropped when it closes. Inside Flatpak the calls go to `org.freedesktop.portal.Notification` (`AddNotification` with a name of the app's own for each notification, `RemoveNotification`, `ActionInvoked`); the action `"default"` is the portal's `default-action`. For this, `PortalHost` and `PlatformDispatcher` have `AppID()`.
- **Main files:** `desktop/notifications.go`, `desktop/services.go` (the binding and the app id in the call); `ui/portal.go`, `internal/engine/engine.go`, `internal/renderhost/renderhost.go` (`AppID`).

## 15.4 System tray

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.4-system-tray
- **Summary:** `desktop.NewSystemTray(icon, child, opts)` is a widget that builds its child and keeps an icon in the system tray (StatusNotifierItem) with a menu (dbusmenu) while it is in the tree. `SystemTrayOpts`: `ID`, `Title`, `Tooltip`, `TooltipBody`, `Status` (`TrayStatusActive`, `Passive`, `NeedsAttention`), `AttentionIcon`, `OnActivate`, `OnSecondaryActivate`, `OnScroll`, `Menu []TrayMenuEntry`. Menu entries: `NewTrayMenuItem(label, onPressed, opts)` (`Disabled`, `Hidden`, `Checkable`, `Radio`, `Checked`, `Icon`), `NewTrayMenuSubmenu(label, children, opts)`, `NewTrayMenuSeparator()`. The icon is a `ui.WindowIcon` (a theme name and/or pictures); `TrayIconFromRGBA(size, rgba)` makes the pictures at 16, 22, 24, 32 and 48 pixels (Catmull-Rom). A worker goroutine exports the objects, takes the name `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-<n>`, registers with `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` (again when the watcher returns), and tells the desktop what a rebuild changed (`NewTitle`, `NewIcon`, `NewAttentionIcon`, `NewToolTip`, `NewStatus`, `LayoutUpdated`); callbacks run on the UI thread. No watcher: `TrayUnavailable`, reported once through the error reporter (the widget is just its child). *For this,* `internal/dbus.Bus` can serve objects: `Export`, `Unexport`, `EmitSignal`, `RequestName`, `ReleaseName`; `dbus.Properties` serves `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties` with `PropertiesChanged`; `fakebus` implements them and has `Invoke` (a call from another connection to what was exported), `Signals`, `Names`, `Take`, `Exported`.
- **Main files:** `desktop/tray.go` (the widget, the model, the worker, `StatusNotifierItem` and `dbusmenu` objects), `desktop/tray_menu.go` (entries, the numbered tree, layouts); `internal/dbus/bus.go`, `props.go`, `fakebus/fakebus.go`.

## 15.5 `examples/tray`

- **Date:** 2026-10-20
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.5-tray-example
- **Summary:** `examples/tray` is a window with a note field and a status line, and a tray icon (drawn in code and scaled by `desktop.TrayIconFromRGBA`) whose menu has "Show window", "New notification", "Open file…", a separator and "Quit"; a click on the icon shows the window. Closing the window (the exit request of `AppLifecycleListener.OnExitRequested`) is answered with Cancel and the window is minimized, so the app stays in the tray; "Quit" sets a flag and asks for a required exit. "New notification" shows the note as a notification with an "Open" action (and the default action), which bring the window back; "Open file…" calls `desktop.OpenFiles` from `State.Go` and shows the path (or "Open cancelled."). *For the tests,* `gluttertest` has `Tester.FakeDesktop()`: a fake notification service, StatusNotifierWatcher and FileChooser portal on the fake bus, with `Notifications`, `TrayMenu`, `TrayProperty`, `ClickTrayMenuItem`, `ActivateTray`, `InvokeNotificationAction`, `CloseNotification`, `PendingFileChoosers`, `AnswerFileChooser`, `CancelFileChooser` and `WaitFor` (SPEC §17); `desktop.InstallBus` is its seam.
- **Fixed on the way (two bugs of 15.1 that the fake bus could not show, found by running the example against a real bus):** (1) `services.connect` opened the session bus with a context that it cancelled when the call returned, and godbus closes a connection when the context it was made with ends, so on a real desktop every call after the first failed with "use of closed network connection". The connection now gets a context that never ends, and only the wait for it is bounded (the call's `ctx`, and `connectTimeout`). (2) `portalMissing` looked for a `*godbus.Error`, and a real bus gives a `godbus.Error` value, so "no such service" was not recognized: `OpenURI` did not fall back to `xdg-open`, and the dialogs, notifications and tray reported other tags than `FileChooserUnavailable`, `NotificationsUnavailable` and `TrayUnavailable`. It handles both now. Tests against a real `dbus-daemon` (`desktop/tray_bus_test.go`: `TestTheSessionBusStaysOpen`, which failed with the old code, and `TestMissingServicesOnARealBus`) keep both fixed.
- **Main files:** `examples/tray/main.go`, `tray_test.go`; `gluttertest/desktop.go`, `desktop_test.go`; `desktop/install.go`; `desktop/services.go`, `file_chooser.go` (the fixes).

- **Summary:** the AT-SPI2 bridge (16.1) gets the interfaces `Text`, `EditableText`, `Value` and `Selection`, and the events of the content. *Text:* the text of a text field by characters (the semantics tree counts UTF-8 bytes; the bridge converts), the caret and the selection (reading and asking the framework to move them through `SetSelection`), parts of the text by character, word, sentence, line and paragraph (`GetStringAtOffset` and the older `GetText{At,Before,After}Offset`). *EditableText:* `SetTextContents`, `InsertText` and `DeleteText` (sent as `SetText`), `CopyText`, `CutText` and `PasteText`. *Value:* sliders, spin buttons and progress bars, with the value read from the text that the framework says; setting `CurrentValue` increases or decreases. *Selection:* the containers whose children say whether they are selected. *Events:* `TextChanged` (insert and delete), `TextCaretMoved`, `TextSelectionChanged`, `accessible-value`, `VisibleDataChanged` and `SelectionChanged`; nodes get and lose their interfaces as their flags change.
- **Found on the way:** the framework gives a text field `SetText` and `SetSelection` only while it has the focus, so the interface `EditableText` does not wait for the action (a field that is not focused would have had none, and the screen reader could never focus and then write); the methods answer false until the field has it, and `GrabFocus` (the `Focus` action) comes first.
