## 17.1 Path boolean operations

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-17.1-path-combine
- **Summary:** `ui.PathCombine(op, path1, path2) *Path` with `ui.PathOperation` (`Difference`, `Intersect`, `Union`, `Xor`, `ReverseDifference`; the zero value is difference), re-exported by `material`. The algorithm (SPEC §12.10 has it in a row): the curves of both paths are cut into lines (uniform steps of the parameter, a tolerance of a ten-thousandth of the size of the paths), every crossing, touch and overlap of two lines becomes a vertex (coordinates snapped to a grid of a billionth of that size, vertices of neighbouring cells welded), which makes a planar graph; each edge has the net number of times each path goes along it; a ray cast from just left of the middle of each edge (with the edges in rows, so that a ray looks at its own row) gives the winding numbers of both paths there, and the other side's follow from the edge's counts; with each path's fill type, an edge is on the border of the result when the operation says differently on its two sides; the edges are chained into contours with the inside on the left (leftmost turn at a vertex where the border touches itself), so a hole turns the other way and the result is valid under both fill types. Where the border follows one of the original curves, the curve comes back: runs of edges that came from the same curve with contiguous parameters are one `QuadraticBezierTo`, `ConicTo` or `CubicTo` (the part of the curve between the first and the last parameter, with its ends on the vertices), and a run of a line one `LineTo`; the contour starts where two runs meet so that a curve is not cut in two. Open contours are closed, as when a path is filled; inputs that cross themselves, overlap, touch along an edge or at a point, are nested, identical, disjoint or empty are all fine; a point that is not finite gives an empty result; a very large number of lines makes the tolerance coarser.
- **Main files:** `ui/path_combine.go`; the generated re-export `material/widgets_reexport_gen.go`.
- **Tests:** `ui/path_combine_test.go`: 75 combinations (15 pairs of shapes × 5 operations: overlapping circles, a circle and a star, two stars, rectangles, rectangles sharing an edge and part of an edge, nested circles, a circle in a rectangle, disjoint, identical circles and rectangles, a ring and a rectangle, a pentagram with each fill type, touching at a corner, tangent circles) compared with the operation on about 2,000 sample points each (away from borders); the areas and the number of contours of the five operations on two squares; that a hole turns the other way and is a hole for both fill types; 12 cases of empty results and of empty inputs (including nil, a point, a line); `NaN` and infinite inputs; the zero operation; that the curves are kept (a circle in a rectangle stays four conics, the border of two circles is conics and every point is on a circle, a quad and a cubic are kept); the same result every time; the inputs do not change; scales from 1e-4 to 1e6 and offsets up to 1e7; 300 pairs of rectangles on a coarse grid obey inclusion-exclusion on their areas; 400 random polygons on a coarse grid that cross themselves and have overlapping and touching edges, with random fill types, all right. `FuzzPathCombine` (no panic, finite points inside the box of the inputs, bounded verbs, finite weights, a result that `Contains`/`GetBounds`/`Flatten` accept): 1.4 million executions in 30 seconds with no failure, and its seeds run with the normal tests. Goldens (`internal/gpu/soft/testdata/goldens/pathcombine-{circles,stars,ring-and-circle}.png`, five cells each: difference, intersect, union, xor, reverse difference), each looked at.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅. Every changed golden image was looked at.
- **Proof:** none listed for this step (the goldens above are the visual check).
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the crossings of curves are found on their lines, so they are off by the tolerance (SPEC §12.10); Skia's pathops would be exact. The result does not merge collinear lines of different original lines. A worst case of long lines that all overlap in x costs time quadratic in their number (bounded by the 32,768 lines).

## 17.2 Raster cache and GPU efficiency

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-17.2-raster-cache
- **Summary:** the GPU renderer does less work, and tells the compositor less. *Raster cache:* the engine turns on `RendererOpts.RasterCacheAfter = 3`, so a layer that was in 3 consecutive scenes as the same object (which `SceneBuilder.AddRetained` gives for the layer of a `RepaintBoundary` that was not repainted) is drawn into a texture in the third scene and by one instance from the fourth (SPEC §9.1, §12.10); `Config.DisableRasterCache` and `GLUTTER_RASTER_CACHE=0` turn it off. *Damage:* `gpu.DamageTracker` hashes a scene into tiles of 64 pixels (each picture by identity, with its transform and the parameters of the layers around it; bounds of the operations from `gpu.ShapeBounds`, `ShadowBounds` and the expanded paragraphs) and reports the tiles that changed from the window's last scene, as at most 8 rectangles; `Context.SwapBuffersWithDamage` presents with `eglSwapBuffersWithDamageKHR` (or EXT) when the display has it. The frame is still drawn whole, so the pixels are the same as without it. Whole-surface cases: the first frame, the same scene again, a size change, a failed swap, a lost X11 window content (`Handler.OnContentLost`, called on `Expose`; the engine calls `Renderer.Invalidate`), an image or backdrop filter, an unknown layer. `Config.DisableDamage` and `GLUTTER_DAMAGE=0` turn it off. *State changes:* `Device` counts the state calls it skipped (and now also caches the clear color), and each `Program` remembers its uniform values (`SetInt`, `SetFloat`, `SetVec2`, `SetVec4`, `SetFloats`, `SetVec4s`), so a steady frame sends almost no uniform; `Device.Stats` has `StateSkipped`, `UniformsSet` and `UniformsSkipped`.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/damage.go`, `bounds.go`; `internal/gpu/gles/{uniforms,renderer,context,egl,device,scene,filters}.go`; `internal/engine/engine.go`; `internal/platform/{platform,nop}.go`, `fake/events.go`, `linux/x11/window.go`.
- **Tests:** *frame counters (fake GL):* with the engine's rule of 3, a retained layer holding a path is drawn as it is in frames 1 and 2, made into a texture in frame 3 (one framebuffer) and drawn by a single instance in frames 4 to 8, with no coverage tile made again after frame 1 and no framebuffer made (`rastercache_test.go`, together with the earlier tests of the rule's details, eviction and the cache's budget); on the framework side, the layers of two `RepaintBoundary`s, one repainted each frame and one not, are the same object in four consecutive scenes for the still one only, and the still painter is called once (`widgets/retained_layers_test.go`). *Damage:* the tracker's frames (first, same pictures in a new scene, a picture recorded again, moved, removed, opacity, the same scene again, a fill with and without a clip, an image filter, size change, `Invalidate`; 20 rectangles merged to one; `damage_test.go`); a property test that renders 250 random pairs of scenes (shapes, strokes, shadows, a mask filter, an image, `drawPaint`, a save layer with a blend mode, rotated rrects, clips, opacity, color filters) with `soft` and checks that every pixel that differs is inside the reported damage (it fails when the opacity is left out of the hash or the bounds are made smaller; `soft/damage_test.go`); that `ShadowBounds` hold the shadows `soft` draws at six elevations; the renderer with the fake EGL: first frame `eglSwapBuffers`, the same pictures a 1 x 1 damage, a changed picture its tiles (with EGL's bottom-left rows), no extension and no option make no damage swap, a failed swap and `Invalidate` present the next frame whole (`gles/damage_test.go`); the engine passes `OnContentLost` to the renderer and reads the two options and variables (`engine/damage_test.go`). *State changes:* uniforms are sent only when they change, per type and array, unknown names ignored, `ResetState` forgets them; the clear color; the counters; a second steady frame sends fewer uniform calls than the first (at most 4) (`uniforms_test.go`). *Display (headless sway, Mesa llvmpipe), tag `glutter_display`:* five frames presented with `eglSwapBuffersWithDamageKHR` are pixel-identical to the same frames without it, and report 1 pixel for the unchanged frame and the two tiles for the moved one; 60 frames with damage and the cache run without a swap error. *X11 (Xvfb):* an `Expose` calls `OnContentLost` and then asks for a frame.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅ · display tests under headless sway and under Xvfb ✅. `examples/gallery` gives the same screenshot with the cache and damage on and off.
- **Proof:** none listed for this step.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** SPEC §12.10 has two rows (the rule of 3 for layers instead of display lists, and the tile hash for damage). The damage only saves the compositor's work: the GPU still draws the whole window (a partial redraw needs the buffer age, `EGL_EXT_buffer_age`, and a scissor to the damage; step 17.4's measurements will say whether it is worth it). A picture that is recorded again but draws the same is damaged (Flutter's layer diff compares layers, which has the same limit for a repainted boundary). The raster cache has no size or complexity test: a small, cheap layer is cached as well, which costs one framebuffer for it; 17.4 will say if a threshold pays.

## 17.3 Debugging aids

- **Date:** 2026-10-21

## 18.1 API review

- **Date:** 2026-10-21

- **Summary:** `glutter-gen apicheck` reads the public packages and checks the conventions of SPEC §12 (SPEC §12.13): the shape of every `NewX` (options only as a trailing variadic value), `child`/`children`/`sliver`/`slivers` last, at most 6 required parameters, the `Flutter:` / `Glutter-specific:` last paragraph of the doc comment of every exported type and function, `Unspecified` as the zero value of an enum, and no exported package variable that holds a map, slice, function or basic value or that its package assigns to. First run: 411 reports. *Fixed:* 14 constructors had `child`/`children` before another required parameter (`NewFocusWithExternalFocusNode`, `NewFocusScopeWithExternalFocusNode`, `NewNotificationListener`, `NewBackButtonListener`, `NewDrawerController`, `NewAdaptiveTextSelectionToolbar`, `NewNestedScrollViewViewport`, `NewKeyedSubtreeWrap`, `NewRepaintBoundaryWrap`, `NewRenderFlow`, `NewRenderCustomMultiChildLayoutBox`, `NewRenderSemanticsAnnotations`, `NewRenderSliverSemanticsAnnotations`, `NewRenderIndexedSemantics`) and now have it last, with every caller and the generated re-exports updated; four constructors took a required options struct (`NewRouteInformation`, `NewDrivenScrollActivity`, `NewMultiFrameImageStreamCompleter`, `NewButtonStyleButtonBase`) and now take `opts ...XOpts`; 13 types had no `Flutter:` line; `desktop.TraySizes` is unexported; `EditableTextDebugDeterministicCursor` is `DebugOptions.DeterministicCursor`; `EditableTextGroupID` is a struct value. *Accepted* (45, in `cmd/glutter-gen/apicheck.allow` with reasons, rows in SPEC §12.10): 12 constructors that have more than 6 required parameters in Flutter, 31 enums whose zero value is Flutter's default or that are results, events or states, and the two const tables `ElevationToShadow` and `MaterialEdges`. A variadic parameter of another type is accepted as Flutter's optional positional parameter (`NewCatmullRomCurve(points, tension ...float64)`).

## Fix: flickering search bars (hover and press), and a keep-alive error

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** fix/search-flicker (a report from the user, not a step of `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md`)
- **Summary:** the user saw the inside of the search bars flicker when hovering or pressing them, and an error in the log. *The flicker:* the raster cache and the other layers (opacity, blur) drew wrong when the engine drew into the window, because the fragment shaders found their pixel with `gl_FragCoord`, and under Mesa's llvmpipe `gl_FragCoord.y` was upside down in a draw into a layer's framebuffer when the window's framebuffer was the one under it (a rectangle in a cached layer came out one row high; a blur came out off). While a bar's hover or press highlight repaints, its text and icons are in layers that the cache makes and then draws, so the hint text was missing from the frames that used the cache and present in the others (a gallery screenshot under sway at the time shows the search bars without their "Search" hint). Every shader now takes the position of the pixel from a varying set by the vertex shader (`vDev`, the device position of the quad), rounded to the pixel center in `devicePixel()` (without the rounding, pixels whose center is on an edge went the wrong way); the filter pass has its own. No test saw it before because every display test drew into a framebuffer of its own (`renderGPU`), not the window's. *The error:* `ParentDataWidgetIncorrectUse` for `KeepAlive` was reported when an `InkResponse` was removed while it had a hover and a pressed highlight: the keep-alive mixin released its handle before the state's `Deactivate` disposed the highlights, so disposing the first highlight asked for a new handle and sent a notification from a deactivated element. `StatefulElement.Deactivate` now runs the state's hook first and the mixins' after, as Dart's `super.deactivate()` at the end does.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/gles/shaders/{paint.glsl,shape.vert.glsl,image.vert.glsl,layer.vert.glsl,mask.vert.glsl,vertices.vert.glsl,filter.vert.glsl,filter.frag.glsl}`, `widgets/component_element.go`, `widgets/state_mixin.go`.
- **Tests:** `internal/gpu/gles/window_display_test.go`: a retained layer (a rectangle, a rounded rectangle and a circle, inside an opacity layer, under a clip) drawn through the window's framebuffer with the raster cache on matches the software renderer in each of 5 frames, with a cached layer made in frame 2 and drawn after; an opacity layer and a blurred layer in the window match the software renderer (without the fix the cached layers lose their contents, 1,800 pixels in the first case, and the blur differs in 3,000). `TestInkWellRemovedWithTwoHighlightsReportsNoError` in `material` (without the fix it reports the error). The existing parity tests (gradients, shapes without anti-aliasing) caught the first version of the shader change and set the rounding.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `go generate ./...` stable ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅ · display tests of `gles`, the engine and the Wayland platform under headless sway, and of `gles` and the engine under Xvfb ✅.
- **Proof:** none listed; a screenshot of the search page under sway after the fix shows the hint texts.
- **Manual checks:** done by the user on their desktop: the search bars no longer flicker on hover or press.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the explanation (Mesa keeping the orientation of the window's framebuffer) is an inference from the symptoms: the same draw gave the same GL state, uniforms and instances in both paths, and only the rows of `gl_FragCoord` differed. The user's GPU may not be llvmpipe; the shader change does not depend on the driver. An error in the middle of a frame with a layer that has image filters panics with "the framebuffer was already released" and hides the error, because the layer's framebuffer is released by `composite` and again when the frame ends (seen while the filter shader was broken); not fixed here.

The tests of the system fonts (`TestBundledFonts`, `TestScanMatcher`, the fontscan case of `TestFallback`) skip on js with the reason "fontscan has no system font directories on js"; `widgets/settings_linux_test.go` and the Linux-only engine, `gles` and platform tests are not built for js.
  - Two races that the single-threaded wasm runtime showed, fixed in the tests and the tester: `Tester.PumpFrame` calls `runtime.Gosched()` so that the goroutines of the app (an image that decodes) post their results (without it the gallery page's `InkImage` stayed blank on js), and `TestShowDialogResultAndBarrier` waits up to a second for the channel that `convertChan`'s goroutine fills instead of reading it with `default`.
  - The Linux `go:build` lines of the test files in `internal/platform/linux/...` are explicit; the other test files that only run on Linux use the `_linux_test.go` suffix. `gles.NewRenderer`, `gles.Open` and `gles.X11Visual` exist on Linux only until the web renderer (step 21.4) adds its own.

## 19.2 Choosing the renderer

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-19.2-choosing-the-renderer
- **Summary:** the engine chooses its renderer by `RunAppOpts.Renderer` (`engine.Config.Renderer`) or `GLUTTER_RENDERER`, with fallback, while `gles` is still the only renderer on Linux. An empty value or `auto` tries the OS's candidates in order at the first frame: a candidate is kept once it has presented the first frame, otherwise its error is logged once at Info level (with its tag) and the next one is tried; if all fail, the last error is returned. A renderer asked for by name never falls back. `RendererUnknown` (not a renderer of Glutter) and `RendererUnavailable` (a known one this OS or build lacks; `vulkan` until step 20.2) are returned before the display is touched. `gpu.SurfaceHandle` gained `Surface` (the `wl_surface` on Wayland, the window ID again on X11). The first-frame log line, the "renderer chosen" line and the `GLUTTER_FRAME_STATS` lines name the renderer and its device (`gles: llvmpipe (LLVM 22.1.8, 256 bits)`).
- **Main files:** `internal/engine/renderers.go` (new: `chooser`, `newChooser`, `rendererCandidate`, `RendererEnv`), `engine.go`, `timings.go`, `backends_{linux,js,other}.go` (`rendererCandidates`, `glesRenderer.Describe`); `internal/gpu/surface.go`; `internal/gpu/gles/renderer.go` (`DeviceName`); `internal/platform/linux/{wayland,x11}/window.go`; `widgets/run_app.go` (`RunAppOpts.Renderer`); `docs/SPEC.md` (§9.6, §13), `README.md`.
- **Tests:** `internal/engine/renderers_test.go`: `TestChooser` (8 cases: auto uses the first candidate, an empty value is auto, by name, auto falling back once and twice with one log line per failure at Info level, every candidate failing returns the last error, a name never falls back, a name skips the candidates before it; each checks which renderers were made, which one drew all 3 frames, that a failed one was closed once and the used one is closed by `Close`, and `Describe`), `TestChooserDelegatesReleaseAndInvalidate`, `TestNewChooserErrors` (5 cases, route tests for `RendererUnknown` and `RendererUnavailable`), `TestDrawWithNoCandidates`, `TestRunChoosesTheRenderer` (4 cases: the environment variable, the option over the variable, `auto` over a name, and the log names the renderer and device), `TestRunRendererErrors` (3 cases, the error comes before the display and the renderers are touched), `TestRunWithEveryRendererFailing`; `TestFrameLogsNameTheRendererAndItsDevice`; the Wayland and X11 tests check `SurfaceHandle.Surface`. 0 Flutter test cases ported (no Flutter counterpart).

Two choices that the sketch left open (SPEC §9.3 says so): every uniform binding takes a dynamic offset, and an entry point "reads" a binding when its name is in its body or in a function it calls (found by text, which the tests cover; `naga` still validates the shader itself). ## 20.1 Vulkan loader, instance and device

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.1-vulkan-device
- **Summary:** Vulkan is loaded through purego and draws into offscreen textures, as an `explicit.Device`. `vulkan.Open(Options)` loads `libvulkan.so.1` (`GLUTTER_VULKAN_LIBRARY` overrides it), binds the function table (global and instance functions through `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, device functions through `vkGetDeviceProcAddr`, the core name first and then the `KHR` one), makes the instance (with `GLUTTER_VULKAN_VALIDATION=1`: the validation layer and the one debug-utils callback, logging through the logger and recording errors), chooses the physical device (`GLUTTER_VULKAN_DEVICE`, the CPU rule), and makes the device and its queue. Buffers, textures, samplers, pipelines (from the SPIR-V of step 19.3), bind groups, passes with dynamic rendering, copies and `ReadTexture` work; the memory allocator uses 64 MiB blocks with a free list, textures are filled through a staging ring, and there are 2 frame slots with command buffers, fences and descriptor pools.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/vulkan/`: `doc.go`, `consts.go`, `structs.go`, `vk.go` (the function table), `arena.go` (the C-memory arena), `check.go` (`vkError`), `choose.go` (device choice), `instance.go`, `device.go`, `memory.go`, `frames.go`, `resources.go`; `.golangci.yml` (the mirrors of Vulkan structs are exempt from `unused`, as x11's are); `docs/SPEC.md` §9.4.
- **Tests:** `header_test.go` compiles a C program against `/usr/include/vulkan/vulkan_core.h` and compares the size and every field offset of the 66 Go mirrors of Vulkan structs (`TestStructLayouts`), and 120+ constants (`TestConstantsMatchHeader`; it found a wrong structure type value); `TestNoFunctionTakesAStructByValue`; the table binding (`TestBindReportsAMissingSymbol` with its `SymbolMissing` route, the extension names, optional functions, the levels); `TestLoadFailed` (route `Open->loadLibrary.VulkanLoadFailed`); the arena (alignment, zeroing, growth, reuse after reset, mark and rewind, strings); the allocator (free list: coalescing, alignment, first fit; memory type choice, 8 cases; blocks shared per type and kind, the big block freed when empty; reuse), `GPUOutOfMemory` from `vkError` and from a fake backend (route tests); `TestChooseDevice` (22 cases over fake lists of physical devices: order, version, extensions, features, texture size, queue family, the CPU rule, the selector by index and by name, and the errors `VulkanNoDevice` and `VulkanUnsupported`); `TestVkError` (5 cases: `GPUOutOfMemory`, `VulkanDeviceLost`, `VulkanCallFailed`). **Display tests** (`glutter_display`, they need Vulkan but no display; they run on lavapipe with validation on and fail on any validation error): the device is lavapipe; clear and read back in RGBA and BGRA; solid rectangles (the overlap, the dynamic uniform offset, the origin, the scissor); blending; the blit of an uploaded texture with a row pitch (upright picture); `CopyTexture`; 9 frames over the two slots; many bind groups; an upload of 16 MiB (larger than a slot's staging); mip levels and samplers; resources destroyed twice; the errors (`VulkanFrameOpen`, `VulkanFrameNotOpen`, `VulkanPassNotEnded`, `VulkanForeignResource`, `VulkanWriteOutOfRange`, the three invalid-description tags, `VulkanSurfaceFailed`, `GPULimitExceeded` on the real device, `VulkanNoDevice` for a CPU device that is not allowed and for a selector that names nothing); the validation layer's messages reach the messenger (a deliberate invalid call) and the messenger is unregistered at `Close`. 0 Flutter test cases ported.

No process is left running (lavapipe runs inside the test).

- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - Textures stay in the `GENERAL` layout, with one global barrier after passes, copies and uploads, instead of a layout per use (SPEC §9.4 says so); a tracked layout can come later if profiling asks for it. Step 20.2 needs `PRESENT_SRC` for swapchain images.
  - A resource is released when the fence of the frame being recorded (or the last one submitted) is done, which relies on the queue finishing frames in order.
  - `ReadTexture`'s `done` runs at the end of `Submit`, after waiting for the fence, not in a later frame: the renderer's `Snapshot` and the screenshot need the pixels at once on Vulkan (SPEC §9.3).
  - The dynamic-rendering dependencies below Vulkan 1.2 (`VK_KHR_depth_stencil_resolve`, `create_renderpass2`, `multiview`, `maintenance2`) are enabled when the device has them; this machine has only Vulkan 1.4 drivers, so that path is not run, and the choice of the version (1.1 with the two extensions) is tested only over fake lists.
  - `lavapipe` allocates descriptor sets without a limit, so growing a frame's descriptor pools (`VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY`) is not exercised by a test.
  - `Device.NewSwapchain` returns `VulkanSurfaceFailed` until step 20.2; `explicit.Device` is not wired into the engine's candidates yet (step 20.7).

## 20.2 Vulkan windows: surfaces and swapchains

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.2-vulkan-windows
- **Summary:** a Glutter window presents through Vulkan on Wayland and X11. `vulkan.Open` takes `Options.Surface` (the `SurfaceHandle`), enables the surface extensions of its kind, makes a `VkSurfaceKHR` (Wayland `Display` + `Surface`, Xlib display + window), requires `VK_KHR_swapchain` and a presenting queue family, and implements `Device.NewSwapchain`: the format (BGRA8 or RGBA8 unorm, sRGB-nonlinear space), the present mode order (mailbox, immediate, FIFO), `minImageCount + 1`, recreation at a new size, and `VK_KHR_incremental_present` damage. `explicit.Renderer` is the skeleton of the engine's renderer: a frame texture, the clear to the background, the blit to the swapchain image, present with damage, the retry once on `explicit.SwapchainOutOfDate`, `Snapshot` and `GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT` through `ReadTexture`. `GLUTTER_RENDERER=vulkan` selects it (no fallback, and a CPU device is allowed when it is named).
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/vulkan/{surface,swapchain}.go` and the changes to `consts.go`, `structs.go`, `vk.go`, `choose.go`, `device.go`, `frames.go`, `resources.go`; `internal/gpu/explicit/{errors,renderer}.go`; `internal/gpu/explicit/fakedevice` (acquire errors, name, completing reads at submit); `internal/engine/{backends_linux,engine}.go`; `docs/SPEC.md` §9.4.
- **Tests:** *vulkan (unit):* `TestChooseSurfaceFormat` (5 cases), `TestChoosePresentMode` (4), `TestSurfaceExtensions`, `TestSurfaceAndSwapchainErrors` (8 cases, route tests of `VulkanSurfaceFailed`, `VulkanSwapchainFailed`, `GPUOutOfMemory`, `VulkanDeviceLost`, `SwapchainOutOfDate`), `TestCreateSurfaceNeedsTheNativeWindow` (4), `TestChooseDeviceNeedsTheSwapchainForWindows`; the layout and constant tests of `header_test.go` now also cover the surface and swapchain structs (with the Wayland and Xlib platform defines). *explicit (fake device):* `TestDrawStagesAFrame`, `TestSecondFrameReusesEverything`, `TestResizeMakesANewFrameTexture`, `TestOutOfDateConfiguresAgainAndRetriesOnce`, `TestOtherAcquireErrorsAreReturned`, `TestPresentDamage`, `TestSeveralWindowsShareTheDevice`, `TestCloseDestroysEverythingOnce`, `TestDrawErrors`, `TestIsSwapchainOutOfDate`. **Display tests** (`glutter_display`, lavapipe, validation on, any validation error fails): `TestWaylandWindowPresentsItsBackground`, `TestWaylandResizeNeverPresentsTheOldSize` (the order of SPEC §8.11: `ack_configure`, the swapchain at the new size, then the present; the compositor never sees a buffer of the old size after the ack), `TestWaylandTwoWindowsShareTheDevice`, `TestX11WindowPresents`. 0 Flutter test cases ported.

- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - `vulkan` comes after `gles` in the engine's candidate list, so only `GLUTTER_RENDERER=vulkan` picks it until step 20.7 sets the default order.
  - A swapchain is recreated or destroyed after `vkDeviceWaitIdle`, so the semaphores of old images are never in use when destroyed (the validation layer reported this otherwise); a resize is not a hot path.

## 20.3 Shapes and rect clips on Vulkan

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.3-vulkan-shapes
- **Summary:** the explicit renderer draws every analytic shape through Vulkan: rect, rrect, oval, circle, DRRect, rsuperellipse, lines, points and `drawColor`/`drawPaint`, filled or stroked, in solid colors with `srcOver`, `dstOver`, `plus` and `dstOut`, cut to rectangle clips by the scissor and the shader's exact clip coverage. The code of `gles/shapes.go` that does not depend on GL moved into `internal/gpu`: `Affine2D`, the instance layout and `ShapeEncoder` (the shape, stroke and paint logic, returning the name of a feature when a shape needs the coverage atlas), `FixedBlendOf` and `PaintOf`; `gles` wraps the encoder, so both renderers make the same instances. `shaders/shape.wgsl` is the port of `shape.{vert,frag}.glsl` and `sdf.glsl`. ## 20.4 Paths, clip masks, images and text on Vulkan

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.4-vulkan-paths-images
- **Summary:** the explicit renderer draws general paths, arcs and every shape without an analytic form from the coverage atlas (8-bit pages of 2048 pixels, tiles of at most 256, cached by shape, linear transform, fractional translation and stroke), text (the glyph paths that `gpu.Flatten` makes of a paragraph), rounded-rectangle, superellipse and path clips through clip masks (an 8-bit texture over the clip's bounds, multiplied into the coverage), images with mipmaps (`drawImage`, `drawImageRect`, nearest, bilinear, a mip level for a downscale, bicubic), nine-patches, sprites without colors and `drawVertices`. The mip levels are made by a downsampling pass, which needed `Texture.Level(i)`: a texture over one level of another, that a pass draws into and a bind group samples (Vulkan: a view for each level). The pure parts of `gles/paths.go`, `clipmask.go`, `images.go` and `vertices.go` moved into `internal/gpu` (`MaskCache`, `ShapeOf`, `ClipCoverage`, `ImageEncoder`, `VertexTriangles`, …) and both renderers use them. Shaders: `mask.wgsl`, `image.wgsl`, `vertices.wgsl`, and `shape.wgsl` now multiplies the clip mask in. Each draw call has its own entry in the uniform ring (clip mask rectangle; for vertices also the paint, clip and blend), bind group 1 is the clip mask and group 2 the atlas page or the image with its sampler.

## 20.5 Gradients, blend modes and layers on Vulkan

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.5-vulkan-effects
- **Summary:** the explicit renderer draws gradients (linear, radial, two-point conical and sweep, every tile mode, up to 32 stops, dithered), image shaders (tile modes, nearest, bilinear, mip level, bicubic), color filters (mode, matrix, gamma, inverted colors), every blend mode (Porter-Duff modes in the pipeline's blend state, the others in the shader from a copy of the region under the draw), `SaveLayer`, and the opacity, color-filter and clip layers of a scene (pooled RGBA8 textures sized to 64-pixel granules, composited by the `layer` pipeline). The paint of a draw became `gpu.PaintSpec`, shared with `gles`, together with its gradient ramp, image-shader and color-filter code. `glutter-gen shaders` now expands `//#include` lines, so `paint.wgsl.inc` (the 55-vec4 `Paint` uniform and its functions) and `blend.wgsl.inc` (ported from `blend.glsl`) are shared by `shape`, `mask`, `image` and `vertices`; `layer.wgsl` is new. Sprites with colors and vertices blended by any mode are drawn now. Color emoji painted with gradients are drawn.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/paintspec.go`; `internal/gpu/explicit/{frame,primitives,layers,pool,scene,resources,slot,renderer}.go`, `shaders/{paint.wgsl.inc,blend.wgsl.inc,layer.wgsl,shape.wgsl,mask.wgsl,image.wgsl,vertices.wgsl}` (`.spv` and `shaders_gen.go` regenerated); `cmd/glutter-gen/internal/shaders` (includes); `internal/gpu/gles/{paintspec,shapes,scene,layers,filters}.go` (they use `gpu.PaintSpec`); `internal/gpu/gputest/effects.go` (the effect scenes, now shared by both renderers); `docs/SPEC.md` §9.3.
- **Tests:** *shaders generator:* `TestIncludesAreExpanded`, `TestIncludeErrors`. *gpu:* `TestRampStops` (4), `TestRampPremultipliedAt`, `TestSetGradient` (5 + the matrix), `TestSetImageShader`, `TestSetColorFilter` (5). *explicit (fake device):* `TestGradientsSetThePaintUniform` (the uniform's shader, transform, geometry, flags, blend and ramp), `TestBlendsThatReadTheDestinationCopyIt` (the copy rectangles and the passes around them), `TestLayersAreDrawnIntoTexturesAndComposited` (the pooled texture, its frame uniform, the composite), `TestNestedLayersAndCulling`, `TestRectOfACopyIsFromTheTargetsCorner`; the unsupported-feature, gradient, blend, color filter, sprite, vertices and layer cases of the earlier tests changed to what is drawn now (`TestUnsupportedFeatures` keeps image filter, backdrop filter, shader mask and mask filter). *gles:* the paint tests use the shared `gpu.PaintSpec`; the table of `TestDisplayPaintsAndLayersMatchSoftware` moved to `gputest.EffectScenes`. 0 Flutter test cases ported. **Display tests** (`glutter_display`, lavapipe, validation on, any message fails): `TestVulkanGradientAndBlendScenesMatchSoftware` (`gradients`: largest difference 1 level; `blend-modes`: every one of the 29 cells at most 15 levels, the same tolerances as `gles`, nothing skipped), `TestVulkanEffectScenesMatchSoftware` (the 8 effect scenes: gradient tile modes, matrix and degenerate gradients, image shaders, color filters, blend modes on shapes, paths, images and vertices, vertices with shaders, save layers with nesting and scene layers; largest difference 24 levels, in the nested layers) and `TestVulkanProofScenesMatchSoftware` (`text-tour` now has its emoji drawn; only the shadow's blur is skipped).

- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - The paint uniform is 880 bytes in every draw call's ring entry (four 256-byte slots), which makes gradient-heavy frames use more of the ring than step 20.4's; the ring grows when needed.
  - A blend that reads the destination copies the region once per call and ends the batch, so a frame full of such draws is slower than one with fixed-function blends (the same as `gles`). Step 20.6 measures the frame times.
  - Image filters, backdrop filters, shader masks and the blur (mask filters, shadows) stay unsupported until step 20.6.

## 20.6 Effects, raster cache, snapshots and full parity on Vulkan

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.6-vulkan-parity
- **Summary:** the explicit renderer draws everything `gles` draws. Blurs: a paint with a mask filter on a rectangle, rounded rectangle, oval or circle (the shape of every `BoxShadow`) is one instance of the shape pipeline's new `KIND_SHADOW`, the closed form of the blur (`shadow.wgsl.inc`); any other shape is drawn white into a layer that `filter.wgsl` blurs and the `layer` pipeline fills with the paint. Image filters (blur, dilate, erode, matrix, color, compose) of a paint, a `SaveLayer` or a scene layer run as filter passes over the layer, backdrop filters copy the region under the layer and filter it into the layer's texture, shader masks paint their shader into the layer, and `Canvas.drawShadow` is an ambient and a spot shadow, each a blurred layer, with the occluder cut out. The raster cache (`RendererOpts.RasterCacheAfter`, set to 3 by the engine) keeps the texture of a layer that was in the last three scenes and draws it with one instance. `Renderer.Snapshot` and `RasterizeScene` (`ui.Rasterizer`) draw a scene without a window. Damage was already wired into `VK_KHR_incremental_present` (step 20.2); `FrameStats` now reports it. What `gles` and the explicit renderer plan the same way moved into `internal/gpu`: the filter passes, the shadow plan, `PaintAccess`/`WhiteFill`/`StyleCode`, and the raster cache policy (`LayerCache[T]`).
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/{filters,effects,layercache}.go`; `internal/gpu/explicit/{effects,layers,scene,frame,renderer,snapshot}.go`, `shaders/{filter.wgsl,shadow.wgsl.inc,layer.wgsl,shape.wgsl}` (`.spv` and `shaders_gen.go` regenerated); `internal/gpu/gles/{filters,effects,rastercache,layers,scene}.go` (they use the shared code); `internal/gpu/gputest/{effects,proof}.go` (the proof tolerances and retained frames now shared by both renderers); `internal/engine/backends_linux.go` (the raster cache for Vulkan); `docs/SPEC.md` §9.3.
- **Tests:** *gpu:* `TestBlurPasses` and `TestFilterPassesOfEveryFilter` (moved from `gles` with the code), `TestLayerCacheEviction` and `TestLayerCacheBoundary` (moved, over a fake texture type). *explicit (fake device):* `TestMaskFilterOnARectIsOneShadowInstance` (the instance's kind, deviation and style, and the padded quad), `TestMaskFilterOnOtherShapesUsesABlurredLayer`, `TestMaskFilterWithNoBlurDrawsTheShape`, `TestImageFilterOfASaveLayerRunsPassesOverTheLayer` (the pass uniforms in the ring: kind, axis, sizes, deviations, kernel), `TestImageFilterOfAPaintFiltersWhatItDrew`, `TestBackdropFilterCopiesWhatIsUnderTheLayer`, `TestShaderMaskPaintsTheShaderIntoTheLayer`, `TestShadowIsMadeOfBlurredLayers`, `TestEveryFilterPipelineIsMadeOnce`, `TestRasterCacheKeepsRetainedLayers` (frames 1 to 5: drawn as they are, drawn into the kept texture, then one instance; one layer texture made), `TestRasterCacheIsOffByDefault`, `TestSnapshotDrawsWithoutAWindow`, `TestSnapshotFailures` (4 cases, strictly as route tests: `RendererNotAttached`, `RendererSizeInvalid` twice, `RendererClosed`), `TestDamageIsCountedInTheFrameStats`; `TestUnsupportedFeatures` now lists a perspective transform and a gradient of more than 32 colors (the effects are drawn). 0 Flutter test cases ported. **Display tests** (`glutter_display`, lavapipe, validation on, any message fails): `TestVulkanEveryProofSceneMatchesSoftware` (all 8 proof scenes within the tolerances of `gputest.ProofTolerances`, which `gles` uses too, nothing skipped: `effects` at most 14 levels, `decorations` 34, `text-tour` 2, with a snapshot of each scene equal to the frame where it is opaque), `TestVulkanSnapshotIsPremultipliedOnTransparent`, `TestVulkanToImageThroughTheGPU` (`Picture.ToImage` through the renderer), `TestVulkanRasterCacheDrawsWhatTheLayerDrew` (no clip, rectangle clip: identical frames; ## 20.7 Vulkan by default, with GLES as the fallback

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-20.7-vulkan-default
- **Summary:** the candidates of `auto` on Linux are `vulkan`, then `gles`. A Vulkan whose only device is a CPU (lavapipe) is not used unless asked for by name, so `auto` gives GLES there; every fallback before the first presented frame is logged once with the renderer and the error's tag (the chooser of step 19.2). A lost device (`VulkanDeviceLost` or `GPUDeviceLost`) is handled in `explicit.Renderer.Draw`: everything that belongs to the device is destroyed, a new device is opened for the same windows and the frame is drawn again; a second loss within 10 seconds returns the error, which ends `RunApp`. `RendererOpts.Now` and `RendererOpts.Log` serve the tests and the log. The README has the runtime requirements and `GLUTTER_RENDERER`. Found while trying the multiwindow example on a real GPU: closing a window with the mouse pointer inside it left the framework's mouse tracker without the pointer's removal (the platform's event arrives after the view is gone and is dropped), so the next added event, in another window, failed the tracker's check in debug builds; the engine now removes the pointer while the view still exists.
- **Main files:** `internal/engine/{backends_linux,engine}.go`; `internal/gpu/explicit/renderer.go`; `README.md`; `docs/{SPEC,PERFORMANCE}.md`.
- **Tests:** *explicit (fake device):* `TestDeviceLostMakesEverythingAgainOnce` (a new device, the old one closed, the window's swapchain made again, the frame drawn; a second loss within ten seconds returns `VulkanDeviceLost` and opens nothing), `TestDeviceLostAfterTheWindowIsRecovered` (three losses spaced over ten seconds, four devices), `TestOtherErrorsAreNotDeviceLoss` (`GPUOutOfMemory` keeps the device), `TestDeviceLostBeforeTheDeviceOpensIsAnError`. *engine:* `TestLinuxAutoTriesVulkanThenGLES`, `TestWithoutVulkanAutoUsesGLESAndLogsTheFallbackOnce` (the real Vulkan candidate with a library that does not exist, then a working GLES; one log line with `tag=VulkanLoadFailed`), `TestVulkanByNameWithoutVulkanIsAnError` (`VulkanLoadFailed` strictly as a route test), `TestClosingAWindowUnderThePointerRemovesThePointerFirst` (3 cases). 0 Flutter test cases ported. **Display tests** (`glutter_display`, headless sway): `TestDisplayWithoutVulkanAnAppFallsBackToGLES` (`VK_DRIVER_FILES` pointing at a file that does not exist), `TestDisplayAutoNeverUsesACPUVulkanDevice` (lavapipe and `auto` give GLES), `TestDisplayVulkanByNameMayUseTheCPUDevice` (lavapipe and `GLUTTER_RENDERER=vulkan` give `vulkan: llvmpipe`).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `GOOS=windows`/`darwin` vet of the engine ✅ · `go generate ./...` changes nothing ✅ · apicheck 0 violations ✅ · display tests of `internal/gpu/...`, `internal/engine` and `internal/platform/linux/wayland` under headless sway ✅ · `glutter_release` and `glutter_profile` tests ✅. No compositor, X server or app is left running.

(The first run of multiwindow found the pointer bug above; after the fix, new window, open dialog and close the dialog work.) The user did not report the GPU's name or numbers.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - **Performance exception, approved by publishing.** The task asks that Vulkan is not more than 10% slower than GLES on any metric, measured with both renderers. Only the software devices could be compared here (llvmpipe and lavapipe): Vulkan's raster time is 49% higher on average and its cold start 18% higher, its worst frame and memory lower (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`). The comparison on a GPU was not recorded; the user approved publishing the step without it. It stays in "Pending" in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.

## 21.2 Web input

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-21.2-web-input
- **Summary:** Mouse, touch, stylus, wheel and keyboard input work on the web as Flutter web delivers them, and `examples/counter` takes three taps and `examples/scrolling` a wheel scroll. `pointerdown`/`move`/`up`/`cancel`/`leave` become `PointerData` through Flutter's button sanitizer and pointer converter (add, hover and move synthesized, `setPointerCapture` on down, one device per touch `pointerId`, the stylus and the mouse with fixed IDs, coalesced moves); `wheel` is converted from lines and pages to pixels with Flutter's trackpad detection and answers `preventDefault` from the framework; `keydown`/`keyup` go through Flutter's `KeyboardConverter` with tables generated by `glutter-gen keys -web-out` (modifier synthesis, CapsLock and key guards on macOS and iOS), and `preventDefault` comes from `DispatchKeyData`. Cursors map to CSS as in Flutter web, the host is focusable, and `WidgetsBinding.BrowserContextMenu()` (`services.BrowserContextMenu`) turns the browser's context menu off and on, doing nothing off the web. Every conversion is plain Go over plain values, so it runs under Node; the engine got `platform.SyncInputHandler` so that a key or a wheel event is handled at once and the answer is there when the browser's callback needs it (SPEC §23.3).
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/web/{pointer,keyboard,keymap_gen,cursor,devevents}.go` (plain Go), `{input_js,devevents_js}.go`, `platform_js.go`, `window_js.go`, `queue.go`; `internal/platform/web/synthetic/` (synthetic DOM events, js only); `internal/platform/web/inputtest/` (the browser test program); `internal/platform/sync.go` (`SyncInputHandler`, `ContextMenuController`); `internal/engine/engine.go` (`OnKeySync`, `OnPointerSync`, `SetBrowserContextMenuEnabled`); `ui/platform_dispatcher.go` (`ContextMenuHost`); `services/browser_context_menu.go`; `widgets/{binding,widget_state}.go`; `cmd/glutter-gen/internal/keys/{keys,web}.go`; `internal/webtest/await.go`; `cmd/glutter-web` (`shot -events -after`); `docs/SPEC.md` §23.4 ("Decided in step 21.2"), §12.10, §14.1.

## 21.3 Web text input, IME and clipboard

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-21.3-web-text-input
- **Summary:** Text fields work on the web. While a text field of the framework has the focus, the platform keeps a transparent `<input>` (or `<textarea>` for a multiline field, `type=password` for hidden text) in the host, placed at the caret rectangle with the caret's height as its font size, with the browser focus; the browser types, composes and pastes into it and `beforeinput`, `input`, `compositionstart`/`update`/`end`, `selectionchange` and `paste` become `ui.TextInputEvent`s through a plain-Go model (`TextEditor`) that finds the change against what the framework holds. `inputmode` and `enterkeyhint` are set on iOS and Android as Flutter does, `autocapitalize` and `autocorrect` from the hints. The clipboard is `navigator.clipboard` (copy and cut write inside the user's key event, a read continues in a `then` callback that posts to the UI goroutine, so keys sent while it is pending are handled), and the browser's paste shortcut is left to the browser, whose `paste` event brings the text without a permission. Characters that nothing handles are typed once by the framework and their keydown is prevented, so the browser does not type them again.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/web/{textstate,textconfig,texteditor,textkeys,clipboard}.go` (plain Go, tested in the normal run and under Node), `{textinput_js,clipboard_js}.go`, `window_js.go`, `platform_js.go`, `input_js.go`, `errors.go`, `devevents{,_js}.go`; `internal/platform/web/synthetic/` (`TextField`, `TypeText`, `DeleteBackward`, `StartComposition`/`Compose`, `Paste`); `internal/platform/web/texttest/` (the browser test program); `ui/text_input.go` (`TextInputEnterKey`, `TextInputState.EnterKey`, `TextInputEvent.DeleteSelection`); `services/{platform_text_input_control,text_input}.go`; `widgets/binding.go`; `internal/platform/sync.go` and `internal/engine/engine.go` (`OnTextInputSync`); `docs/SPEC.md` §23.5 ("Decided in step 21.3"), §12.10, §14.1.
- **Tests:** **42 Flutter test cases ported**: 12 from `composition_test.dart` (the three handlers of `CompositionAwareMixin`, seven 'determine composition state' cases, the two 'composing range' cases) and 30 from `text_editing_test.dart` (`EditingState`: flipped offsets, default composing offsets, min and max, reading an `input` and a `textarea`, the three comparisons, negative offsets; `TextEditingDeltaState`: insertion, backward and forward deletion, deletion of a selection, composing region replacement, double space to a period, accent menu, plus deletion and new line at an inverted selection, as the event of the input method in place of the delta; the element configuration: password, non-default text action, autocorrect off and on, multi-line, the four capitalizations, and `inputmode` for Android, Firefox on Android and iOS) as table tests of the plain-Go conversions (`textstate_test.go`, `textconfig_test.go`, `texteditor_test.go`). Written for this step: `TestUTF16Conversions` (7 + 7), `TestHandleTypingAndEditing` (12), `TestHandleKeepsTheFrameworksViewOfTheText`, `TestHandleComposition` (6 steps and 4 cases), `TestSetState` (8), `TestPaste` (4), `TestDiffEdit` (7), `TestFieldBoxOf` (3), `TestEnterKeyHintAttribute` (8), `TestIsNativePasteKey` (12), the clipboard with a fake API (`clipboard_test.go`: no API, a read answered from the promise's callback and not before, a failed read, a read ended by its context once, writes, kinds and formats), `TestErrorRoutes` (5 new tags with their routes), `TestParseDevEvents` (4 new steps and 4 new failures), `TestTextFieldWithoutAPage` (route of `SyntheticTextFieldNotFound`, under Node); `services`: `DeleteSelection` (4 cases), `TestPlatformControlEnterKeyOfTheAction` (14), the result of `HandleUnhandledKey`; `engine`: `TestSyncTextInputIsHandledAtOnceAfterWhatWaits`; `widgets`: `TestBindingReportsAKeyTheTextFieldTookAsHandled`. **Browser tests** (`glutter_browser`, Chromium and Firefox): `TestBrowserTextInput` (`internal/platform/web`, with `texttest` and `webtest.Await`): a tap on a `TextField` makes an `<input>` with the focus, synthetic `beforeinput`/`input` events type "hello" and a `deleteContentBackward` deletes, a `compositionstart`/`compositionupdate`/`compositionend` sequence shows "ni" as composing text (range 4..6, element holds it) and then commits 你好 (no composing range left), a `paste` event is prevented and its text inserted, the A key is prevented and typed once, Control+V is not prevented and changes nothing (the browser pastes), three keys sent while a stubbed `navigator.clipboard.readText` is pending are all handled and the read is not answered, then the stub's promise resolved answers the read, a rejected one is `WebClipboardReadFailed`, `SetData` calls `writeText`, Control+A and Control+C copy the selection, the password field gives `type=password`, the multiline field a `<textarea>` where Enter makes one line break, and without a focused text field the element is gone and the host has the focus.

The owner ran `go run ./cmd/glutter-web serve ./examples/editor` in a browser: the first run showed `ClipboardStatusCheckFailed` (the text field asked the browser to read the clipboard to decide whether to show Paste; fixed by `NewWebClipboardStatusNotifier`, Flutter's `_WebClipboardStatusNotifier`, which the web uses so that the clipboard is never read before a paste), and typing was very slow, which is the `soft` renderer drawing the whole window in wasm for every key (about 17 to 50 ms natively for a 640x480 scene, several times that in wasm); the GPU renderers of steps 21.4 and 21.5 are what fixes it. **Still to do by the owner:** try an IME (IBus or Fcitx5 with a Chinese or Japanese input method) in Chrome and in Firefox, once the page is fast, and record the answers here. (No real IME, virtual keyboard or physical clipboard was used by the tests: they dispatch synthetic events from a goroutine of the program, which is the path of the browser's own events but not the real thing, and replace `navigator.clipboard` by a stub.)
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** (decisions are in SPEC §23.5 "Decided in step 21.3" and three rows of §12.10)
  - **Same contract as Linux, so the framework keeps the caret and the selection.** Flutter's web engine sends whole editing states or deltas and turns the framework's text shortcuts off (`kIsWeb`), letting the browser edit; here the element sends only the text change and the composing text (`TextEditor`), and a selection that only the browser moved (the cursor gestures of some mobile keyboards) is not sent. The ported tests of the delta inference are ported as events of the input method; the delta state itself is not ported, because the contract has no delta.
  - **Additions to shared code, all additive:** `ui.TextInputEvent.DeleteSelection` (a soft keyboard's Backspace over a selection commits nothing but removes it), `ui.TextInputState.EnterKey` (from the `TextInputAction`), `platform.SyncInputHandler.OnTextInputSync` (so the framework's echo is in the element before the next event is read), and `TextInput.HandleUnhandledKey` returns whether it took the key, which makes `OnKeyData` answer true for a character the framework typed: the Linux backends ignore the answer; the web uses it to prevent the browser's own typing.
  - **The paste shortcut goes to the browser:** Control+V, Control+Shift+V and Shift+Insert (not on macOS and iOS, where the browser's is Command+V and Control+V pastes nothing) are not given to the framework while the field has the focus, so the browser fires `paste`, which needs no permission. A paste by the toolbar or by the app is `navigator.clipboard.readText`, which Chrome may ask the user about.
  - **`compositionend` commits at once** (Flutter waits for the next event). `inputmode` and `enterkeyhint` are set only on iOS and Android, as in Flutter; `TextInputType.none` turns the input method off (as on Linux) instead of keeping a field with `inputmode=none`.
  - **Not done:** autofill, Safari's order of events (`compositionend` before the last `input`), and no iOS or Android browser was available to try the virtual-keyboard attributes (only the unit tests cover them).
  - **New tags** with route tests: `WebClipboardReadFailed`, `WebClipboardWriteFailed`, `WebClipboardFormatUnsupported`, `SyntheticTextFieldNotFound`; the web clipboard also returns `ClipboardPrimaryUnavailable` and `ClipboardReadTimeout`. `WebClipboardUnavailable` now means no `navigator.clipboard` (an insecure context).
  - **Debug-only scripted events** gained `input:`, `compose:` and `paste:` (they act on the hidden field).

## 21.4 WebGL 2 through gles

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-21.4-webgl
- **Summary:** The `gles` renderer draws on the web through WebGL 2, with the same shaders (GLSL ES 3.00 as they are), the same device, pools, caches and scene code. The GL function table is split in two bindings of one interface (`glAPI`): `gl_purego.go` (Linux, the former `gl.go`) and the new `gl_js.go` over `syscall/js` (every context method bound once and called with `Invoke`, one reused `Uint8Array`/`Float32Array` for uploads, uniforms and read-backs, a `js.Value` per GL object kept in a plain-Go `handleTable`). `context_js.go` makes the context from the page's canvas (`getContext("webgl2", {alpha, premultipliedAlpha, antialias: false, depth/stencil: false, preserveDrawingBuffer: false, ...})`) behind a small imitation of EGL (`webEGL`), so `context.go`, `Renderer` and `Device` are unchanged for Linux: no swap, no damage (frames are drawn whole), the canvas size is set before a frame (`Context.ResizeSurface`), and a browser-lost context (`webglcontextlost` with `preventDefault`, `webglcontextrestored`) drops and remakes the device and every cache, draws the next frame whole, and asks the engine for a frame. The web renderer list is now `webgl`, then `soft`; before each try after the first the engine has the platform put a new `<canvas>` in place (`platform.SurfaceRenewer`, `window.RenewSurface`), because a canvas keeps the first kind of context it was asked for. `auto`, `GLUTTER_RENDERER=webgl|soft` (query parameter) work as on Linux; `gles`/`vulkan`/`webgpu` on the web are `RendererUnavailable`.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/gles/{gl_purego.go (renamed from gl.go), gl_js.go, context_js.go, handles.go, webgl.go, context.go, renderer.go}`; `internal/gpu/gles/glwebtest/` (the browser test program); `internal/engine/{gles_renderer.go (shared engine renderer over gles, moved out of backends_linux.go), backends_js.go, backends_linux.go, engine.go, renderers.go}`; `internal/platform/sync.go` (`SurfaceRenewer`), `internal/platform/web/{window_js.go, platform_js.go}`; `internal/webtest/{browser.go, procgroup_linux.go, procgroup_other.go}` (`--enable-unsafe-swiftshader`; a private Xvfb for Firefox); `docs/SPEC.md` §9.1 ("Decided in step 21.4").
- **Tests:** 0 Flutter cases ported (no Flutter counterpart). Plain Go (normal run, `-race`, and under Node): `TestHandleTable` (4 lookups, then removal, reuse and null), `TestWebContextAttributes`, `TestLossState` (5 sequences), `TestWebErrorRoutes` (4 tags with routes: `WebGLCanvasNotFound`, `WebGL2Unavailable`, `WebGLSurfaceKindUnsupported`, `WebGLContextLost`), `TestIsES3AcceptsWebGL2` (5), `TestOpenWithAWebHandleUsesTheWebPlatform`, `TestRendererResizesASurfaceThatHasItsOwnSize`, `TestRendererWhileTheContextIsLost` and `TestRendererRebuildsAfterTheContextIsRestored` (a fake EGL that can lose and restore its context: nothing drawn or touched while lost, the device, the caches and the raster cache made anew after, the new context filled, nothing leaked after `Close`), `TestContextRebuildNeedsALossyContext`, and **`TestBindingsHaveTheSameFunctions`** (reads `gl_purego.go`, `gl_js.go` and `glapi.go` as source and fails if a binding lacks a function of the interface; checked by renaming one method). ## 21.5 WebGPU

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-21.5-webgpu
- **Summary:** The explicit renderer draws on the web through WebGPU. `internal/gpu/webgpu` is an `explicit.Device` over `navigator.gpu` through `syscall/js`: `Acquire` awaits the adapter, the device and the compilation of every WGSL module at startup (the web's `connectDisplay` calls it before the platform installs its listeners, SPEC §23.3), and nothing after that waits for a promise. The canvas's `webgpu` context is the swapchain, `writeBuffer` and `writeTexture` go through one reused `Uint8Array`, `ReadTexture` finishes in a later task (`mapAsync` completed from a callback that posts to the UI goroutine), and `Snapshot` is drawn by `soft`. A lost device (`device.lost`) takes the explicit renderer's existing `GPUDeviceLost` path, with a new device asked for without waiting (the new `GPUDevicePending`). The web renderer list is `webgpu`, `webgl`, `soft`.

- **Manual checks:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** (decisions are in SPEC §9.5 "Decided in step 21.5")
  - **The headless Chromium flags are three, not one, and WebGPU runs on the real GPU.** `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` alone gives SwiftShader's adapter, whose canvas swap chain cannot be created in headless mode (the GPU process logs `Could not find SharedImageBackingFactory ... WebgpuSwapChainTexture` and the device is destroyed at the first `getCurrentTexture`; the same with `--use-angle=swiftshader`, `--use-vulkan=swiftshader`, `--ignore-gpu-blocklist` and `--ozone-platform=x11` under headless). `--enable-features=Vulkan` and `--use-angle=vulkan` together give the adapter `amd rdna-3` and a working canvas (each alone does not). Non-headless Chromium on a private Xvfb also works, but was not needed. Consequence: the WebGPU tests ran on this machine's GPU through Mesa RADV and nothing was seen on a software adapter or on another vendor's driver; on a machine with no Vulkan GPU headless Chromium has no WebGPU adapter that can present, and the tests would fail for it (not skip). Chromium's WebGL 2 now also runs on the GPU through ANGLE (it was SwiftShader in step 21.4's tests), which the existing WebGL tests and goldens did not mind.
  - **Firefox 158 on Linux has WebGPU** behind `dom.webgpu.enabled` (set in the profile's `user.js`, with its reason) and passes every test here, with the same numbers as Chromium. The tests still skip Firefox, with the probe's reason, when a build has no adapter.
  - **The startup device is awaited by the engine, not by the platform.** `connectDisplay` (web) calls `webgpu.Acquire` before `web.New`, so before any listener, when the renderer is `auto` or `webgpu`; its error is kept and returned from the renderer's first frame, which is what lets `auto` fall back and a named renderer fail. The chooser's candidate list, `RendererUnavailable`, the log lines and the `renewSurface` hook of step 21.4 are as they were.
  - **A mid-frame loss is silent until the browser tells.** `device.lost` is a promise, so the renderer notices the loss at the next `Begin`, `Submit`, resource call or swapchain call after the callback ran; a frame recorded in between draws into a destroyed device and does nothing, and a capture asked in that frame ends with `WebGPUReadFailed` (or `GPUDeviceLost`). The recovery of the next frame is tested. A new device that the browser refuses is `WebGPUDeviceFailed` from the next frame and ends the app; the last resort of switching the page to WebGL 2 is step 21.6, as is `auto` choosing at the first frame with the loader showing errors.
  - **Validation errors of the browser are asynchronous.** A pipeline whose layout does not fit its shader, or a call that breaks a WebGPU rule, is reported to the page's `uncapturederror` event in a later task and the frame goes on; `Provider.ValidationErrors` collects them, the log shows the first twenty, and the browser tests fail on any (none was reported). The shaders are checked at startup (`getCompilationInfo`), pipelines are not.
  - **Not done:** an out-of-memory error of the browser (`GPUOutOfMemory`) is async too and is not mapped; the queue's `onSubmittedWorkDone` is not used (destroying a resource after its submit is safe in WebGPU); Firefox's frame times; no real-GPU run on another vendor.
  - **Added shared code, all additive:** `explicit.Shaders`, `explicit.GPUDevicePending`/`IsDevicePending`, `RendererOpts.OnCapture`; the engine's `Config.post`, `captured`, `webgpuOpen` and `webgpuClose` (unexported, set by `Run` or the web's `connectDisplay`). The glwebtest program hides `navigator.gpu` for its engine modes, so the `gles` browser tests keep testing WebGL 2 and soft.

## 21.6 Web fallback, GPU loss and services

- **Date:** 2026-10-21
- **Branch:** feat/step-21.6-web-fallback
- **Summary:** Steps 21.4 and 21.5 had already built most of the choice and the recoveries (the list `webgpu`, `webgl`, `soft` tried at the first frame with a new canvas before each try after the first, the WebGL 2 context restoration, the WebGPU device loss with `GPUDevicePending`); this step adds what was missing. WebGPU's last resort now works at run time: the chooser's candidates have an optional `SwitchOn`, and a `webgpu` frame that fails with `GPUDeviceLost` (a second loss within ten seconds) or `WebGPUDeviceFailed` (a new device the browser will not give) closes the renderer, has the platform put a new canvas in place and draws the same frame with `webgl` (then `soft`); `GLUTTER_RENDERER=webgpu` by name never switches and ends `RunApp` with the error. The loader now puts a failed start (non-zero exit code) into the page, in `#glutter-message`, with the tag-bearing lines of what the program wrote. `desktop.OpenURI` (`window.open(uri, "_blank", "noopener")`, `javascript:`/`vbscript:` refused) and `desktop.ShowNotification`/`CloseNotification` (Notifications API: permission request, click, close, replace by tag, time-out) work on the web through a plain-Go `web.Desktop` with a thin `syscall/js` layer; the file dialogs and the tray return their Unavailable tags without trying D-Bus.

  - **Named renderers never switch (SPEC §9.6).** `GLUTTER_RENDERER=webgpu` ends `RunApp` with `GPUDeviceLost` or `WebGPUDeviceFailed`, as `GLUTTER_RENDERER=vulkan` does; only `auto` switches. Recorded in SPEC §9.5/§9.6 and §12.10.
  - **The notification of the web is smaller than Linux's (SPEC §12.10):** no buttons (a service worker is needed), only the action `"default"` as the click; `BodyMarkup` is stripped to plain text; a theme icon name is ignored (a URL or path is used); `Category` and `AppName` have nowhere to go; the `Timeout` is a timer of the page that closes the notification with `NotificationClosedExpired`; a close the page cannot explain is `NotificationClosedUnknown`. "Asks for permission once" is read as once per decision: a permission that stays `default` (the prompt dismissed) is asked for again at the next call, as the browser allows.
  - **`javascript:` and `vbscript:` URIs are refused** with the new `OpenURISchemeBlocked` (they would run script in the page); every other scheme, `mailto:` included, goes to `window.open(uri, "_blank", "noopener")` as SPEC §23.7 said. `noopener` makes `window.open` answer `null`, so a pop-up blocker's refusal is not detectable and not reported.
  - **The tests of the web services stub the browser's objects** (`window.open`, `Notification`) because a headless browser cannot answer a permission prompt or allow a real window; the code under test is the real one. No real permission prompt, notification center or pop-up blocker was exercised, and no real user gesture (the stubs do not need one): the manual behavior of a real Chrome and Firefox is not covered.
  - **New tags, each with a route test:** `OpenURISchemeBlocked`, `NotificationPermissionAborted`, `WebNotificationFailed`, `DBusUnavailableOnWeb` (route test in `desktop`, as the cause of `FileChooserUnavailable` and `TrayUnavailable`); `NotificationsUnavailable` and `OpenURIUnavailable` are the existing Linux tags, now also from the web.
  - **The loader's message** takes the last four lines that are not Info, Debug or Warn log lines (each cut at 300 characters) because the engine's error line carries a stack: the tag is in its first characters. `Result.Shown` of `internal/webtest` carries the text of `#glutter-message` to the tests. The loader now keeps the last 64 KiB of the program's output always (it kept the first 64 KiB, and only with `glutter_report`).

## 22.1 Fonts loaded at run time

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.1-load-fonts-at-run-time
- **Summary:** An app can load TrueType and OpenType fonts under a family name while it runs: `PlatformDispatcher.LoadFontFromList`, `services.FontLoader` (bytes, functions or assets) and `RunAppOpts.Fonts` (bytes or an asset of `Assets`, loaded before the first frame). A family can hold several fonts; `Match` ranks them by the weight and slant that the font tells (a variable font counts for every weight of its `wght` axis), and a loaded font wins over a bundled one of the same name. After a load the engine forgets what it resolved, and the binding lays the text out again (`PaintingBinding.SystemFonts` → `SystemFontsDidChange` on every render object that has it).
- **Main files:** `internal/text/fonts.go` (`AddFont`, `Generation`, `LoadedPrefix`), `internal/text/layout/engine.go` (`LoadFontFromList`, cache by generation), `ui/platform_dispatcher.go` (`LoadFontFromList`, `OnFontsChanged`), `ui/text_style.go` (`FontLoadingEngine`), `services/font_loader.go`, `rendering/binding.go` (`HandleSystemFontsChange`), `widgets/binding.go`, `widgets/run_app.go` (`FontSource`, `RunAppOpts.Fonts`), `internal/renderingtest` (`NewTextEngine`), `material/widgets_reexport_gen.go`, `docs/GUIDE.md` (section 11), SPEC §12.10.
- **Tests:** table tests for `AddFont` (order for regular, bold, italic and bold italic requests; the family inside the font; the same bytes twice; a copy of the data; loaded before bundled; four tagged failures with route checks); the engine (a family before and after loading, as the first family, as a fallback, and as a fallback for a glyph the first font lacks; weights; the failure route); the dispatcher (four cases and the notification); `FontLoader` (order, assets, failing sources, cancel, reuse); `loadFontSources` (11 cases, with route checks); a `RenderParagraph` that is laid out again after `LoadFontFromList` through the binding. Ported from Flutter: 2 cases of `services/font_loader_test.dart`. Go Mono (`golang.org/x/image/font/gofont`) is the monospace font of the tests.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · GOOS=js build and vet ✅ · scripts/test-wasm.sh ✅ · apicheck ✅ (0 violations) · display tests none
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** SPEC §12.10 has the rows: `LoadFontFromList` is a method of the dispatcher and returns an error, not a `Future`; `FontLoader` takes the dispatcher in `Load` and panics when reused; `RunAppOpts.Fonts` replaces the pubspec; the binding walks the render trees on a font change. A TrueType collection is read at index 0. Fallback by family name is step 22.3; `gluttertest` fonts are step 22.2.

## 22.3 Fallback to the listed families first

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.3-listed-families-first
- **Summary:** A style's fonts are now tried as `FontFamily`, then each `FontFamilyFallback` entry in order, then the system default. `text.Collection.Match` gives, for a family that is not generic, only the fonts that belong to it: loaded and bundled ones of that name, and the system fonts of that family or of a name that the matcher says it stands for (`text.Aliaser`). A generic family (`sans-serif`, `serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy`, `emoji`, `math`) still gives the matcher's whole list. So `FontFamily: "Missing", FontFamilyFallback: ["monospace"]` now draws with the monospace font; before, fontconfig's list for the missing family started with the default sans font, which won.
- **Main files:** `internal/text/fonts.go` (`Aliaser`, `IsGenericFamily`, the filter in `Match`, an alias cache), `internal/text/scan.go` (`scanMatcher.Aliases`), `internal/platform/linux/fontconfig/fontconfig.go` (`Config.Aliases`), `internal/engine/backends_linux.go` (the adapter), tests next to each.
- **Tests:** `Match` over a fake matcher that answers like fontconfig (10 cases: installed family, names ignoring case and blanks, missing family, three generic families, aliases, an alias with no font, no aliases asked for a generic family, family plus alias); a matcher without `Aliaser`; aliases asked once; the matcher's error returned unchanged; loaded fonts before system fonts of one family; `IsGenericFamily` (14 cases); the engine with that matcher (9 cases, 5 of which fail when the filter is switched off: missing family with and without a fallback, skipping missing entries, the first family with a font wins, an alias); a paragraph's widths (monospace); the same over the real fontconfig and over fontscan, and `Config.Aliases` over a fake library (5 cases, 2 failure routes, cancel, closed) and over the real library (a family nothing mentions has none; skipped without the library). On this machine `Aliases("Arial")` is `Liberation Sans, Arimo, Albany, TeX Gyre Heros, Helvetica LT Std, ArialMT`. The existing `TestMatchOrder` changed: the system fonts of other families no longer follow a bundled family. No Flutter tests ported (the engine's font manager is not in `reference/`).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · GOOS=js build and vet ✅ · scripts/test-wasm.sh ✅ · apicheck ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** SPEC §12.10's fallback row says what Flutter does not: Skia's fontconfig manager accepts a match when the font's family is the request or a strongly bound substitute; here `Aliaser` finds the substitutes as the names that fontconfig adds for a family and does not add for a family it knows nothing about (the probe), because fontconfig's public API does not tell the binding. A font's first family name is the one compared. Where the default font is itself the alias of a family (Liberation Sans on a system whose default sans is Liberation Sans), the alias is not seen, which changes nothing: the default comes next anyway.

## 22.5 Font queries and the desktop's font settings

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.5-font-queries-and-settings
- **Summary:** An app can ask which face a family resolves to (`PlatformDispatcher.ResolveFont`: family name, file and index, where the font comes from, weight and slant), which families exist (`InstalledFontFamilies`, from fontconfig's `FcFontList`, the font scan, the bundled and the loaded fonts), and which fonts the desktop uses: `PlatformConfiguration.UIFontFamily/UIFontSize/MonospaceFontFamily/MonospaceFontSize` come from the settings portal's `font-name` and `monospace-font-name` of `org.gnome.desktop.interface`, are followed live, and are read with `UIFont()` and `MonospaceFont()`. A change of one of them calls `OnPlatformConfigurationChanged`.
- **Main files:** `ui/text_style.go` (`ResolvedFont`, `FontOrigin`, `FontQueryEngine`), `ui/platform_dispatcher.go`, `internal/text/layout/engine.go` (`ResolveFont`, `InstalledFontFamilies`), `internal/text/fonts.go` (`Collection.Families`, `Lister`), `internal/text/scan.go` (`scanMatcher.Families`), `internal/platform/linux/fontconfig` (`Config.Families`: `FcFontList` and the object set functions), `internal/platform/fontdesc.go` (`ParseFontDescription`), `internal/platform/settings.go`, `internal/dbus/settings.go`, `internal/engine` (adapter and conversion), SPEC §10 and §8.8.

## 22.6 Text benchmarks and an LRU glyph cache

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.6-text-benchmarks-lru-cache
- **Summary:** Benchmarks measure building, laying out and painting a line of 100 columns of monospace text in 5, 10 and 20 styled spans, a page of 50 lines, and the software renderer drawing that page; the numbers are in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. The caches of glyph outlines and of color glyph pictures (16,384 entries each) now drop the least recently used entry when full, where they were emptied. The profile found one local cost, the cache key that `Engine.fontsFor` built with `fmt.Fprintf` for every span: it is now built in a buffer and looked up without allocating (a line of 20 spans: 755 allocations before, 507 after; a page of 50 lines: 28,593 before, 22,377 after).
- **Main files:** `internal/text/layout/lru.go`, `lru_test.go`, `bench_test.go`, `engine.go` (`fontsFor`), `paint.go`, `colr.go`, `paint_test.go`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
- **Tests:** the cache (7 table cases: filling, dropping the oldest without emptying, a hit protects an entry, a put of an existing key, sizes 1 and 0, a miss; the links in both directions; a nil value is a hit); the glyph path cache keeps the outlines in use and drops the least recently used (and makes a dropped outline again); the bound test now checks that a full cache holds exactly its size with the newest entry in and the oldest out; a test that the benchmark input is what it claims (100 columns of Go Mono, one line, n spans).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · GOOS=js build and vet ✅ · scripts/test-wasm.sh ✅ · apicheck ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the time of a build is the cost of a code line (65 to 96 µs, shaping and segmentation); a cache of shaped runs is written under "Pending" in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` and not done. The benchmarks were not run under `GOOS=js`. The machine's times vary by about 15% between runs, so the allocation counts are the evidence of the `fontsFor` change.

## 22.8 `ReorderableListView`

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.8-reorderable-list-view
- **Summary:** Material's reorderable list is ported: `NewReorderableListView(children, ReorderableListViewOpts)` and `NewReorderableListViewBuilder(itemBuilder, itemCount, ReorderableListViewOpts)`. On Linux, Windows and macOS (by `ThemeData.Platform`) every item gets a drag handle (`Icons.DragHandle`) at its end (at its bottom when the list scrolls horizontally) that starts the drag at once, with the grab cursor and the grabbing cursor while an item is dragged (or `MouseCursor`); on iOS, Android and Fuchsia a long press on the item starts it; `BuildDefaultDragHandles: Some(false)` leaves the drag to the app's own listeners. Every item is wrapped in a global key of its own key and the list's state, so an item that moves keeps its state. `examples/scrolling` has a seventh tab, "ReorderView", and the gallery's "Lists & cards" page a section with a vertical list (builder, header) and a horizontal one (children); the gallery's coverage test needs every constructor on a page.
