## 22.9 Tab stops in paragraph layout

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.9-tab-stops
- **Summary:** a paragraph can put each `\t` on the next tab stop, as CSS's `tab-size` does. `ui.ParagraphStyleOpts.TabSize` (a `float64`, a count of the advance of a space in the paragraph's own font; 0, the default, keeps Flutter's behavior) goes through `painting.TextPainterOpts.TabSize` (also `TextPainter.TabSize`/`SetTabSize`, `TextPainterComputeWidthOpts.TabSize`, `GetParagraphStyleOpts.TabSize`). In `internal/text/layout` the width of a rune range is measured from the start of its line (`paragraph.span`), so line breaking, the intrinsic widths, the width of a line, the ellipsis and the hanging white space follow the stops; when a line is built its tab glyphs get the advance of their stop (plus the letter and word spacing of their style), so `GetBoxesForRange`, `GetPositionForOffset`, the glyph infos, the caret, the line metrics and justification see the whole tab. A tab hangs at the end of a line (it never makes a line wrap or longer), a wrapped line starts its stops again, a right-to-left paragraph measures from the right edge, a tab has the paragraph's level (UAX #9 L1) so it is never inside a right-to-left run, and a tab draws nothing when it has stops. SPEC §10 ("Tab stops"), §11.3, §12.10 (a row) and `docs/GUIDE.md` say so; the spec and the plan for 22.9 to 22.11 were added in this step's first commit.
- **Main files:** `ui/text_style.go`, `painting/text_painter.go`, `painting/text_style.go`, `internal/text/layout/tabs.go`, `internal/text/layout/{paragraph,lines,paint}.go`, `internal/text/layout/tabs_test.go`, `painting/text_painter_test.go`, `ui/text_test.go`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md`.
- **Tests:** with Go Mono (every glyph advances the same), against an oracle that measures the text between tabs with paragraphs that have no tabs: a tab at the columns 0 to 9 for the tab sizes 1, 2, 4, 8 and 2.5 (a tab on a stop advances a whole width); several tabs in a row; CJK, emoji, an emoji sequence and combining marks before tabs; styled spans (bold, a bigger tab, letter and word spacing, a span of only tabs); wrapping (the tab that hangs, stops that start again, a tab on a stop, a word wider than the line); the minimum intrinsic width; right-to-left (a right-to-left paragraph, a Hebrew run in a left-to-right one and the levels of the tabs); every query on one line (boxes, the position at the first and second half of a tab, glyph info at and near a tab, the caret at the stop after a tab, line metrics); no glyph drawn for a tab; tab size 0 (as before); an ellipsis and `maxLines`; justification; `TabSizeInvalid` (route tests in `ui` and `layout`); a randomized test of 300 texts with tabs that checks that every tab ends on a stop measured from the left of its line and that the boxes of a line do not overlap; in `painting`, the caret, the position and the boxes through a `TextPainter`, `SetTabSize` and the width helpers.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · GOOS=js build and vet ✅ · scripts/test-wasm.sh ✅ · apicheck ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none for this step
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** SPEC §12.10 has the row (a Glutter addition). `Text`, `RichText`, `RenderParagraph` and `EditableText` do not have the option yet. Positions are measured in logical order, which equals the distance from the start edge because a tab has the paragraph's level; a tab at the very start of a line that is followed by a word too wide for the rest of the line leaves the line with only the (hanging) tab, as pre-wrap does for spaces.

## 22.10 A cache of shaped runs

- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.10-shaped-run-cache
- **Summary:** the text engine keeps the shaped glyphs of each run between builds (`internal/text/layout/shapecache.go`), keyed by the run's text, face, features, direction, script and language and by the context HarfBuzz reads (whether there is text before the run, and, for the scripts that join letters, five runes on each side); the size is not in the key because the engine shapes at one size and scales. It holds 4,096 runs and 8 MiB (a weighted `lruCache`, which also gained `clear` and a lookup by a byte key that does not allocate), is for the UI thread, and is emptied with the engine's other font state when the collection's generation changes (`LoadFontFromList`). To make an unchanged line 5 times cheaper the profile said the shaper was only 27% of a build, so the step also keeps the analysis of each text (bidi levels, pieces by script, UAX #14 segments, clusters, words) in a cache of its own (`analysis.go`, 2,048 texts, 4 MiB) with shortcuts for ASCII left-to-right text (the split by script, with go-text's rules for the ASCII delimiters) and for clusters of text below U+0300; `splitByFace` has an ASCII path that gives `shaping.SplitByFace`'s result without its allocations; `styleFonts` keeps the faces of the ASCII characters in an array and `fontsFor` finds the last eight styles by value; the face's extents are kept; `ui.ParagraphBuilder` keeps one `ResolvedTextStyle` per pushed style (`TextRun.Style` is a pointer, and `Build` hands the runs to the paragraph); and `BuildParagraph` no longer lays the paragraph out (the first query, `Layout` or paint does it, at an infinite width when nothing laid it out): `TextPainter` laid it out again at once. SPEC §10 ("Shaped run cache") and the §12.10 row say so; `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` has the profile and the numbers.
- **Main files:** `internal/text/layout/{shapecache,analysis,lru,engine,shape,paragraph,lines,boxes,geometry,paint,decor}.go`, `ui/text_style.go`, `internal/text/layout/{cache_test,lru_test,bench_test}.go`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- **Tests:** `cache_test.go` builds 400 random paragraphs (Latin, accents and combining marks, ligatures, Hebrew, Arabic, CJK, Hangul, emoji sequences, tabs, newlines, brackets, eight styles with sizes, weights, italics, spacing, features, a locale and a fallback, left-to-right and right-to-left) cold, again from the caches, and with a span changed, moved or removed, and compares every run glyph by glyph (ids, clusters, advances, offsets, metrics) with the pipeline as it was before (a segmenter of its own, `shaping.SplitByFace`, one call of the shaper per run), and the analysis with a fresh one; 150 more are laid out with the caches on and off and the lines, boxes, metrics and draws compared; the fast analysis (levels, pieces, clusters) against go-text on 800 random texts for each of four alphabets, four languages and both directions; the ASCII `splitByFace` against the library on 2,000 random splits; the key (what changes it and what does not); the context test with a system Arabic font (skipped when the machine has none; with the context left out of the key it fails: tried); eviction by the number of runs and by bytes (the oldest first, a hit protects, an oversize run is not kept, a paragraph that overflows a small cache stays correct) and the limits of the spec; `TestFontLoadClearsTheCaches`; the sizes that share an entry; `TestUnchangedLineShapesNothing` counts the runs that reach the shaper (an unchanged line 0, one changed span 1, a page of 50 lines with one span changed 1); that a paragraph is laid out on demand and answers every query as one laid out at an infinite width; the weighted `lruCache`. All the other tests of the repository pass unchanged, goldens included.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · GOOS=js build and vet ✅ · scripts/test-wasm.sh ✅ · apicheck ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none for this step
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the numbers are in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`: an unchanged line's build is 8.4×, 7.9× and 6.1× faster for 5, 10 and 20 spans (4.9, 6.2 and 9.6 µs, from 40.8, 48.5 and 58.4), one changed span shapes one run (14 to 18 µs), and a page of 50 lines where one changed costs 364 µs. **That last goal, "about one line's build", is not met**: each of the 49 lines that did not change still costs about 7 µs (the builder and the engine), so the page is 14 lines of a cold build; only a caller that keeps the paragraphs of lines that did not change can reach it. The context test needs a system Arabic font, so it does not run everywhere. `ParagraphBuilder` cannot be used after `Build` (Flutter says the same), and `ui.TextRun.Style` is a pointer now.

## 23.1 Hiding a window (close to the tray)

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/window-hide
- **Summary:** the owner asked for it so that an app with a tray icon (English Tutor) can close its window to the tray; it was done before it was written into `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md` as step 23.1 (milestone M23). `RegularWindowController.SetHidden(hidden)` and `IsHidden()` take a window off the screen and the task bar and bring it back with its size, title, icon, state and widget tree; `Activate` (and `SetMinimized(false)`) shows a hidden window first. A hidden window still counts as open, so `RunApp` goes on while one exists, and closing it, `ExitApplication` and `RequestAppExit` work as before. The request goes through `ui.PlatformDispatcher.SetWindowHidden` (`ui.WindowControlHost`) to `platform.Window.SetHidden(hidden) bool`: X11 withdraws the window (`XWithdrawWindow`, loaded through purego) and shows it by restoring `_NET_WM_STATE`, `XMapWindow` and `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW`; Wayland attaches a null buffer, destroys the role objects (decoration, dialog, export, `xdg_toplevel`, `xdg_surface`, or the libdecor frame) and makes a new role on the same `wl_surface` to show it, drawing nothing before its configure and ignoring a stale frame callback; the web ignores it (returns false); the fake platform records it. The engine asks a hidden window for no frame and, since the desktop backends report no lifecycle, derives it from the windows: `Hidden` when every window is hidden, `Resumed` when one has the focus, `Inactive` otherwise (after the view focus events of a change). `examples/tray` hides its window on close and shows it from the tray. Released as `v1.5.0` (tagged on `main` and pushed when the owner asked for a version tag); `README.md` and the version line and scope of SPEC §1 and §3 say what 1.5 adds.
- **Main files:** `widgets/window_controller.go`, `ui/window_control.go`, `internal/platform/platform.go`, `internal/engine/engine.go`, `internal/platform/linux/x11/{lib,window,wmstate}.go`, `internal/platform/linux/wayland/{window,decoration,extras}.go`, `internal/platform/linux/wayland/decor/decor.go`, `internal/platform/linux/wayland/fakecomp/windowing.go`, `internal/platform/{fake/window,fake/events,web/window_js}.go`, `internal/renderhost/renderhost.go`, `gluttertest/{tester,windows}.go`, `examples/tray/{main,tray_test}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md`.
- **Tests:** no Flutter test cases (Flutter has no counterpart). `widgets/window_hidden_test.go`: hide, hide twice, show, `Activate` and un-minimize on a hidden window, a destroyed window, widget state kept across hide and show, lifecycle `Hidden` with frames off and back on, exiting with the only window hidden (three ways). `internal/engine/hidden_test.go`: the lifecycle over one and two windows (focus, hide, show, close), a platform that reports its own lifecycle, no frame asked of a hidden window and the waiting one asked on show (presented whole), `Run` going on with a hidden window and ending on exit, focus moving between windows with no `Inactive` in between. A minimized window still counts as visible for the lifecycle (Wayland does not say; X11's `Minimized` is not used yet). Deriving the lifecycle means every Linux app now gets `Resumed` and `Inactive` on focus changes, as Flutter's desktop embedders do. On Wayland a failure to make the new role (only libdecor can fail) ends `Run`. On X11 a hide and show in quick succession does not wait for the window manager to finish the withdrawal, as ICCCM asks. Vulkan on RADV fails at the first frame under headless sway, on `main` too, so the Vulkan runs used lavapipe as SPEC §17 says.

## 25.5 Vulkan on Android, and choosing the renderer

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-25.5-vulkan-on-android
- **Summary:** The explicit renderer draws on Android through Vulkan (`VK_KHR_android_surface`, `libvulkan.so`), and `auto` chooses `vulkan`, then `gles`, then `soft`: Vulkan on Android 10 or later, on Vulkan 1.1, on a driver that is not on Impeller's deny list (ported as a table), once the first frame is presented; the log says what was chosen and, for each candidate that was not kept, why. The swapchain is pre-rotated: its `preTransform` is the surface's `currentTransform`, its images have the size turned for a quarter turn, and the blit pass draws the frame rotated to match (the rotation is the blit's instance index, so the shader needs no uniform); the damage rectangles are rotated the same way, and a swapchain made before the surface was on screen is made again, and the frame blitted again, without drawing the scene. The blit into the swapchain image no longer loads it (`LoadDontCare`). `glutter-android build -vulkan-validation <dir>` packs the validation layer, and `shot -rotation` turns the device.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/vulkan/` (`drivers.go`, `surface.go`, `swapchain.go`, `device.go`, `choose.go`, `consts.go`, `structs.go`, `vk.go`, `frames.go`), `internal/gpu/explicit/` (`device.go`, `renderer.go`, `shaders/blit.wgsl` and its SPIR-V, `fakedevice`), `internal/gpu/webgpu/swapchain_js.go`, `internal/engine/` (`backends_android.go`, `android_vulkan.go`), `internal/platform/android/` (`sdk_android.go`, `log_android.go`, `main_android.go`, `logline.go`), `internal/androidtool/apk.go`, `cmd/glutter-android/` (`commands.go`, `shot.go`), `internal/androidtest/` (`vulkan_device_test.go`, `app.go`), `examples/dev/android-parity/`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10, §24.4 "Decided in step 25.5"), `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`.
- **Tests:** no Flutter test cases for the platform parts; the deny list has the cases of `driver_info_vk_unittests.cc` (Adreno 504 to 650 denied, 660 and 750 not, Mali names, Maleoon) and one for each other rule (31 table cases, the vendor IDs, `VulkanDriverDenied` route). Plain Go: the pre-transform choice (8 cases), the Android surface struct layout and extensions, the API 29 check with its route and the chooser on an old Android (auto falls back with the tag in the log, by name does not), the blit rotation of the renderer for the four rotations, `RotateRects` (6 cases and four turns back), the blit pass not loading the swapchain image, the stale swapchain blitted again, the validation layer packed into each ABI (and the error when it is missing), `-vulkan-validation` and `-rotation`, the layer finder of the harness with its route, and the log end marker.
- **Device tests (`-tags glutter_android`):** on `glutter-37`, with the validation layer: every proof scene through Vulkan, in portrait and in landscape, is within `gputest.ProofTolerances` of the software renderer's image drawn on the device (the gradients seams are exact on Vulkan), nothing skipped, and the layer reports nothing; the counter with Vulkan and with soft in the four orientations gives screens that agree to 2 levels, and the log shows the swapchains made with pre-rotations 1 and 3 (and 2 when the system reports it); `auto` logs the Vulkan device (`Goldfish GFXStream (SwiftShader Device (Subzero))`, API 1.3.0), the swapchain and the choice, with no failed try; on an emulator started with `-feature -Vulkan`, `GLUTTER_RENDERER=vulkan` ends with `VulkanNoDevice` in the log and no fallback, and `auto` logs "renderer not usable" with the Vulkan tag and chooses `gles`. All earlier device tests pass (the GLES test now asks for `gles` by name, since `auto` chooses Vulkan).

- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - The PowerVR rules of Impeller's deny list apply to the vendor ID `0x1010` here; Impeller's never match (SPEC §12.10).
  - The emulator's Vulkan device is a CPU-type device (gfxstream over SwiftShader): `auto` takes it (it passes the deny list, and the CPU rule is Linux's), and `GLUTTER_RENDERER=vulkan` is tried whatever the device.
  - The system reports a surface's transform when it likes; a half turn is often never reported on the emulator, and the compositor then turns the frame (correct, but not pre-rotated). The device test compares the pixels in all four orientations and requires only that some orientation was pre-rotated.
  - Found and fixed on the way: a line written with `log.Fatal` could be lost when the process ended right after it (the pipe to logcat is asynchronous); the standard logger now writes to logcat at once, and `main` returning waits for the pipe to drain.
  - The validation layer comes from the owner's `.android-test/vvl/` (SPEC §24.13); `.android-test/` is not committed.

## 25.6 Touch, mouse, stylus and keys

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-25.6-touch-mouse-stylus-keys
- **Summary:** Android input reaches the framework as Flutter's does: every `MotionEvent` (touch, stylus, inverted stylus, mouse, hover, wheel, the trackpad gestures Android reports) becomes `PointerData` through ports of `AndroidTouchProcessor` and the engine's `PointerDataPacketConverter`, and every `KeyEvent` becomes `KeyData` through ports of `KeyEmbedderResponder` and `KeyboardManager`, with key tables generated by `glutter-gen keys -android-out`. A key the framework does not handle is dispatched again by the activity, and mouse cursors are set with `PointerIcon`. Debug builds take a `GLUTTER_DEV_EVENTS` script (`wait`, `tap`, `swipe`, `key`) that the view dispatches as the user's input.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/android/` (`pointerconv.go`, `touch.go`, `motion.go`, `keyboard.go`, `deadchar.go`, `keymap_gen.go`, `cursor.go`, `devevents.go`, `exports_android.go`, `jni_android.c`, `host*.go`, `window.go`), `cmd/glutter-gen/internal/keys/` (`android.go`), `internal/androidtool/java/.../` (`GlutterView`, `GlutterActivity`, `Native`) and `classes.dex`, `cmd/glutter-android/shot.go`, `internal/androidtest/input_device_test.go`, `examples/dev/android-input/`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10, §24.5 "Decided in step 25.6"), `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`.
- **Tests:** plain Go, in the normal run: the ported cases of the touch processor and the converter (every action, tool type, pointer change, button transition, the synthesized events and their order, hover, scroll, trackpad pan zoom, historical samples), the key responder (down, repeat, up, modifiers and lock synthesis, dead keys and their compositions, the character combiner), the decoding of motion events and what it rejects, the batches `Platform.onMotion` delivers, the answers `onKey` gives, the cursor table, the dev events parser (`AndroidDevEventsInvalid` route), the layout of the generated key tables, and the generator's test.
- **Device tests (`-tags glutter_android`):** on `glutter-37`: an `adb` tap and a swipe arrive as down, move and up of kind touch at the right place; a mouse tap arrives as the trackpad pan zoom; keys of `adb input keyevent` arrive as key data with the right physical and logical keys; a key that a `Shortcuts` handles is taken and one that nothing handles is dispatched again; the dev events script taps like `adb` does (the screens of the counter match); a swipe scrolls `examples/scrolling`.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · GOOS=js build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · device tests ✅

(The mode selector wraps its labels on a phone's width: the example is not adapted to phones in this step.)

  - Historical samples of a move are delivered as moves of their own, the converter has `viewExists` for the delegate, the key responder ignores what Flutter asserts, and dead keys compose without `java.text.Normalizer` (SPEC §12.10).
  - Back is not a key event on a target API of 33 or later; it comes with predictive back in step 25.9.

## 25.8 Text input, the soft keyboard and the clipboard

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-25.8-text-input-clipboard
- **Summary:** Text fields work with the soft keyboard and input methods: `GlutterInputConnection` (a port of `InputConnectionAdaptor` over a `ListenableEditingState`) gives the input method an editing state that it edits at once, and the edits reach the framework as `TextInputEvent`s through the web's plain-Go `TextEditor`; the framework's state is written back unless a later edit is on its way (a number of the edits settles the race of the two threads). The clipboard is `ClipboardManager` (text). The dev events script types: `text:`, `compose:` and `action:enter`.

## 25.10 Fonts on Android

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-25.10-android-fonts
- **Summary:** Text uses the system's fonts and fallback as an Android app does. `internal/text/androidfonts` (plain Go) is a port of Skia's Android font manager: it parses `/system/etc/fonts.xml` and the `fonts_customization.xml` files (the formats of API 26 to 37) and matches a family (names, aliases, weights, styles) with the fallback chain in Skia's order, by language (CJK by locale, with the script inferred), and per character; `engine.SystemFontMatcher` gives it to the `text.Collection` (the bundled Roboto and Material Icons stay first). CBDT/CBLC (and sbix) bitmap glyphs, the emoji font of Android 8 to 12, are drawn by the layout engine, on Android and on Linux. `scripts/fetch-reference.sh` also fetches Skia at the revision Flutter's `DEPS` pins (`reference/skia`).

- **Summary:** Apps are usable with TalkBack. `Platform.Services().Accessibility()` is the Android bridge: the Java side follows `AccessibilityManager` (an accessibility service, touch exploration) and the framework's semantics tree is made while one is on; each `ui.SemanticsUpdate` goes to the main thread as one binary payload (a port of `AccessibilityBridge.updateSemantics`'s data) with every Android-facing property of the nodes already worked out in plain Go (a port of the decisions of `createAccessibilityNodeInfo`); `GlutterAccessibility` (a port of `AccessibilityBridge.java`) keeps the tree, answers the system's `AccessibilityNodeProvider` calls, hit-tests touch exploration, sends the accessibility events (window state and content changes, live regions, scrolling, text, focus) and turns the actions of the services (click, long click, scroll, set progress, cursor moves, set selection, set text, copy, cut, paste, dismiss, expand, collapse, show on screen, custom actions) into `SemanticsActionEvent`s. `GLUTTER_A11Y=1` (debug builds) forces the bridge on, and the dev events script has `a11y:<action>,<label>`.
- **Main files:** `internal/platform/android/` (`accessibility.go`, `accessibility_wire.go`, `accessibility_info.go`, `accessibility_actions.go` and their tests, `platform.go`, `bridge.go`, `devevents.go`, `exports_android.go`, `host_android.go`, `jni_android.c`), `internal/platform/settings.go` (`AccessibleNavigation`), `internal/engine/engine.go`, `internal/androidtool/java/.../` (`GlutterAccessibility.java`, `GlutterView.java`, `GlutterActivity.java`, `Native.java`) and `classes.dex`, `internal/androidtest/a11y_device_test.go`, `examples/dev/android-a11y/`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10, §24.10 "Decided in step 25.11"), `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`.
- **Tests:** Go tables of the plain parts: the wire format (golden bytes, a round trip of every field, every decode failure with its route), about 55 cases of the node info (class names, text composition, actions, range, collection, heading, live region, password, hidden, disabled, links, roles, custom action ids, UTF-16 ranges), every action id and its arguments, the bridge over fakes (the screen reader's state, updates only while on, custom actions kept, reset, a new activity, forcing, close) and the dev events. `AccessibilityBridgeTest.java` needs the Android runtime; its cases are the device tests.
- **Device tests (`-tags glutter_android`):** on `glutter-37` and `glutter-26`, with the bridge forced on: `uiautomator dump` lists the button (clickable, with its bounds), the live text, the text field (an `EditText`), the list (a scrollable `ScrollView`) and its items with their labels; a scripted `a11y:click` on the button increments the count; `a11y:scrollforward` scrolls the list; the change of the live region sends its accessibility event.

## 26.2 The Material text selection toolbar and the magnifier

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-26.2-selection-toolbar-magnifier
- **Summary:** Selecting text on Android shows Material's toolbar, handles and magnifier. `TextSelectionToolbar` (the white rounded bar with its animated overflow menu), `TextSelectionToolbarTextButton`, `TextSelectionToolbarLayoutDelegate` and the Android branch of `AdaptiveTextSelectionToolbar` are ported, and the `TextField`'s default context menu builds them on Android (the §12.10 deviation "the toolbar of every platform is the desktop one" is narrowed to iOS and macOS). `RawMagnifier`, `MagnifierDecoration`, `MagnifierController`, `MagnifierInfo`, `TextMagnifierConfiguration`, `TextMagnifier` and `Magnifier` are ported and used by the selection overlay while a handle, the cursor or a long-press-move is dragged (`TextField`, `EditableText`, `SelectionArea` and `SelectableRegion` take a `MagnifierConfiguration`). To magnify, the renderers read a backdrop through the matrix filter's reverse bounds (`gpu.BackdropMatrix`; `soft`, `gles` and `explicit`). The `DidChangeMetrics` of the editable text reads the view's insets, and a field that loses the focus disposes its handles (two Flutter behaviors that were missing).

## 26.3 Predictive back transitions

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-26.3-predictive-back
- **Summary:** A route follows the back gesture on Android as in Flutter. `PredictiveBackPageTransitionsBuilder` and `PredictiveBackFullscreenPageTransitionsBuilder` are ported from `material/predictive_back_page_transitions_builder.dart` and the Android default of `PageTransitionsTheme` is the predictive builder. While a gesture pops the route the page shrinks, moves with the finger and gets rounded corners over the page below; a button press or a programmatic pop uses the fade-forwards transition. `MediaQueryData` has `DisplayCornerRadii`, and `gluttertest` plays a gesture (`StartBackGesture`, `UpdateBackGestureProgress`, `CommitBackGesture`, `CancelBackGesture`, `PopRoute`) through the same entry points as the platform. The dev events script has `back:hold` and `back:release`.
- **Main files:** `material/predictive_back_page_transitions_builder.go`, `material/page_transitions_theme.go`, `widgets/media_query.go`, `gluttertest/back.go`, `internal/platform/android/devevents.go`, `BackNavigation.java` (and `classes.dex`), `examples/dev/android-back/main.go`, `material/widgets_reexport_gen.go`, the tests `material/predictive_back_page_transitions_builder_test.go`, `material/page_transitions_theme_test.go`, `widgets/media_query_test.go`, `gluttertest/back_test.go`, `internal/platform/android/devevents_test.go`.
- **Tests:** the Dart tests of `predictive_back_page_transitions_builder_test.dart` and the Android cases of `page_transitions_theme_test.dart`, the motion of the shared element (scale, shift and the clamped vertical drag, from both edges), the display corner radii of `MediaQuery`, the gesture of `gluttertest`, and the parser of `back:hold` and `back:release`.

  ![26.3 android predictive back](implemented-proof-images/26.3-android-predictive-back.png)
  `examples/dev/android-back` on `glutter-37` (software renderer) after a tap on "Push the second page" and a scripted back gesture held at one half: the second page (teal) is smaller, has rounded corners, and the home page shows around it.

- **Deviations and follow-ups:**

The page that is pushed in the example has its own color, because two pages of the same color hide the shrinking.
  - No view reports the corners of the display, so `DisplayCornerRadii` stays `None` on Android and the transition uses Flutter's tween (0 to 32 logical pixels).
  - No snapshots (`SnapshotWidget`) and no Cupertino builder.

The cause in the arena (the result with two pointers is not deterministic) is not found; to look at.

## 26.4 Spell check

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-26.4-spell-check
- **Summary:** Misspelled words in a text field are underlined on Android and a tap on one opens a toolbar with the suggestions, as in Flutter. The framework side is ported: `SpellCheckService`, `DefaultSpellCheckService`, `SuggestionSpan` and `SpellCheckResults` (`services/spell_check.go`), `SpellCheckConfiguration` and `BuildTextSpanWithSpellCheckSuggestions` (`widgets/spell_check.go`), the spell check parts of `EditableText` (`widgets/editable_text_spell_check.go`: the check on each change, the composing region, `FindSuggestionSpanAtCursorIndex`, the toolbar), the overlays' `ShowSpellCheckSuggestionsToolbar`, and Material's `SpellCheckSuggestionsToolbar` with its layout delegate and the `TextField` option `SpellCheckConfiguration` (Material style and toolbar on every platform). The engine side is `ui.SpellCheckHost` (the stand-in for the `flutter/spellcheck` channel), which the engine forwards to the window; on Android `SpellCheck.java` (the port of `SpellCheckPlugin`) asks `TextServicesManager` and `spellcheck.go` turns the UTF-16 ranges of the answer into byte offsets. Linux and the web have no spell checker, so it stays off there.
- **Main files:** `ui/spell_check.go`, `internal/engine/spellcheck.go`, `internal/platform/android/spellcheck.go`, `SpellCheck.java` (and `Native.java`, `GlutterActivity.java`, `jni_android.c`, `classes.dex`), `services/spell_check.go`, `widgets/spell_check.go`, `widgets/editable_text_spell_check.go`, `widgets/editable_text*.go`, `widgets/selection_overlay.go`, `widgets/text_selection_overlay.go`, `widgets/text_selection_gesture.go`, `material/spell_check_suggestions_toolbar*.go`, `material/text_field.go`, `gluttertest/tester.go` (`Opts.SpellChecker`), `examples/dev/android-spell/main.go`, the tests next to them and `internal/androidtest/spell_device_test.go`.
- **Tests:** the Dart tests of `services/spell_check_test.dart`, `widgets/spell_check_test.dart` (13 of 13, on Android and iOS), `material/spell_check_suggestions_toolbar_test.dart` (6 of 6), the "Spell check" group of `editable_text_test.dart` and the two spell check cases of `text_field_test.dart`, with the tests of the dispatcher (`ui`), the parser and the requests of the platform, and two device tests: a misspelled word typed with the dev events is found by the system's spell checker, and a tap on it opens the toolbar and a tap on the first suggestion replaces it.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · GOOS=js build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · device tests ✅
- **Proof:**
  ![26.4 android spell check](implemented-proof-images/26.4-android-spell-check.png)
  `examples/dev/android-spell` on `glutter-26` after typing "helo wrld ok" and a tap on "wrld": the word is underlined and the toolbar lists the suggestions of Gboard's spell checker (world, weld, welding) and Delete. (The black underline on the word at the cursor is the keyboard's composing region; Flutter shows the same.)
- **Manual checks:** pending (`docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`, 26.4).
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - See SPEC §12.10 (the spell check rows) and §24.6 ("Decided in step 26.4").

The device test there checks that the request went through the system's service and came back without an error; the words, the suggestions and the toolbar are checked on the API 26 image, and by the manual check on a phone. A misspelled word is red and wavy only while the keyboard is not composing it (the cursor is in another word).

## 27.1 Scroll positions after their Scrollable is gone

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-27.1-scroll-position-disposed
- **Summary:** A `Scrollable` that leaves the tree in the frame after its metrics changed no longer makes the program panic. `ScrollPositionBase` keeps the `WidgetsBinding` it got from the storage context when it was made, and a `disposed` flag set by `Dispose`: a `DidUpdateScrollMetrics` posted before the dispose does nothing, `SaveScrollOffset` after it does nothing, and the debug checks and `post` read the kept binding, never the storage context of an unmounted state.
- **Main files:** `widgets/scroll_position.go`, `widgets/scroll_position_dispose_test.go`, `material/text_field_scrollable_removed_test.go`, `internal/engine/{export_test.go,scrollable_removed_test.go}`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10, the `ScrollContext` row).
- **Tests:** `TestScrollPositionAfterDispose` (3 cases: the posted `DidUpdateScrollMetrics`, `SaveScrollOffset`, and `SaveScrollOffset` with `RestoreScrollOffset`, against a scroll context whose storage context panics once unmounted); `TestTextFieldInScrollableTakenOutByTheWidth` (3 cases, `gluttertest`: a `TextField` in a scroll view that the app takes out when the window narrows); `TestScrollableTakenOutAfterItsMetricsChanged` (2 cases) runs the framework in the real loop of the engine over the fake platform (`engine.RunOnFake` from `export_test.go`): the first layout posts `DidUpdateScrollMetrics`, the next frame takes the `Scrollable` out, and the posted function runs after it. The engine test and the unit test were run against the old code and fail there with the `StateContextUnmounted` panic of the report. Flutter test cases ported: 0 (flutter_test runs microtasks inside `pump`, which hides the case).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - The plan says "a function that a position posted does nothing once `disposed` is set". That holds for `DidUpdateScrollMetrics`, but not for `post` itself: an activity that another position absorbed (`Absorb` after `updatePosition`) ends through the `post` of the position it came from, and that position is disposed in a posted function right after. Making `post` skip then would leave the new position ballistic forever. `post` keeps working after `Dispose`, through the kept binding; the activities already check their own `disposed` flag in `end`.
  - Looked at every other deferred call of a position, an activity and a `ScrollableState`: the activities' `end` (own flag), `ForcePixels`' post-frame callback (touches only the position's own field), the old position's `Dispose` (posted while the state is mounted), the scrollbar's post-frame check and fade-out timer (`Mounted()` and `Dispose` cancel), the selection delegate's post-frame callback (`Dispose` clears its flag), `NestedScrollViewState.handleHasScrolledBodyChanged` (`Mounted()`). None needed a change. `nestedScrollController.scheduleUpdateShadow` reads the coordinator state's context, but only from `Attach` and `Detach`, which run while the inner scrollable is alive, and a child is disposed before its parent.
  - `engine.RunOnFake` lives in `export_test.go`, so the framework can run in the engine's real loop from `package engine_test` (the framework imports the engine, so the test cannot be in `package engine`).

## 27.2 `gluttertest`: unmount the tree at the end of a test, and a fake desktop without a file chooser

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-27.2-gluttertest-unmount
- **Summary:** `gluttertest.New` registers a cleanup (`Tester.unmountTree`) that pumps an empty widget with a `UniqueKey`, so every `State.Dispose` runs and every `State.Lifetime` is cancelled at the end of a test, as flutter_test does. It does nothing when the test failed already (`Failed() bool` of the `TB`; `*testing.T` has it), when the framework reported an error that the test did not take, or when no widget was pumped. An error that the unmounting reports fails the test. `FakeDesktop.DisableFileChooser()` takes the file chooser portal away (`fakebus.Bus.Unhandle`), so `OpenFiles` (files and folders), `SaveFile` and `SaveFiles` fail with `FileChooserUnavailable`.
- **Main files:** `gluttertest/{tester,desktop,doc}.go`, `internal/dbus/fakebus/fakebus.go` (`Unhandle`), `material/dropdown.go`, `widgets/{selection_container_test,navigator_tags_test,export_test}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10 and §17).
- **Tests:** `gluttertest/unmount_test.go`: disposal and the cancelled lifetime after a `t.Run` subtest; table of a passing test, a test that failed already, an untaken error (the tree is left alone), and an error while unmounting (fails the test, with the tag); a cleanup registered after `New` still sees the tree; nothing to unmount without a widget. `gluttertest/desktop_test.go`: `TestFakeDesktopWithoutAFileChooser` (4 cases, route `OpenFiles->call.chooseFiles.FileChooserUnavailable` and the like, with the `method` metadata) and `TestFakeDesktopFileChooserWorksUntilItIsDisabled`. Flutter test cases ported: 0 (flutter_test's own harness is not in `reference/`).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Time of `go test -race ./...`** (`-count=1 -p 3`, compiler capped, same machine): **before 2m51s real (8m57s user); after 2m39s real (6m31s user)** on a warm build cache. The first run after the change took 3m42s because it recompiled `widgets`, `material` and their dependents; no slowdown is measurable.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - SPEC §12.10 has a new row for the order: Flutter runs the tear-downs after the unmounting, but `t.Cleanup` runs last in, first out, so a cleanup registered after `New` runs before it (the plan wants that, so a cleanup still sees the tree). An object that the tree uses and that the test disposes is registered before `New`.
  - **Tests that broke, and what each was** (none weakened):
    - Four `SelectionContainer` tests (`TestSelectionContainerUpdatesItsRegistrar…`, `…SwappingOutContainerDelegateDoesNotCrash`, `…CanUpdateWithinOneFrame`, `…GetsRegistrarFromContextIfNotProvided`) disposed their delegates in a cleanup that ran before the unmounting (a test that relied on the tree outliving its delegates); they make the tester after registering those cleanups. Flutter's tests do the same through `addTearDown`.
    - **A real bug:** `dropdownButtonState.Dispose` dismissed the menu route, which completed the route's future at once and ran the `PoppedThen` callback inside the dismissal (`NavigatorLocked`). Flutter runs it as a microtask; it now goes through `WidgetsBinding.Post`, as SPEC §12.10 says for microtasks (3 `TestDropdownButtonStates` cases and `TestMenuErrors/dropdown_opened_while_open` failed).
    - `TestNavigatorTagsOfThePublicAPI` and `TestTransitionRouteTags` trip the navigator's checks in the middle of a change of the history, which leaves it locked on purpose (Flutter never unlocks it); `navTagsApp` registers a cleanup that unlocks it (`NavigatorState.ForceUnlockHistory`, in `widgets/export_test.go`) for the unmounting. The `NavigatorLocked` case also leaves a half-installed route, so it unmounts inside the test and takes the errors that this reports.
  - `TagFileChooserUnavailable` stays unexported: the tag is public by its documented name, like the other `desktop` tags, and the tests match it by route.

## 27.5 Closing and destroying the first window

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-27.5-first-window-close
- **Summary:** The first window closes like the others when the app wants it to. `WindowingOwner.SetImplicitWindowDelegate(d)` gives the delegate that is asked when the user closes the first window (with the controller); without one it stays a request to exit the app. `ImplicitWindowController().Destroy()` removes the first window: the window is closed, the view leaves the dispatcher, and the `View` of the implicit view builds an empty `ViewCollection`, so its content is taken out of the tree and its states are disposed; the other windows go on, and the app ends with the last window (the platform's loop stops when none is left). A window that the platform closed (the exit request was allowed) takes the same way, through the new `PlatformDispatcher.OnViewRemoved`. `examples/multiwindow` keeps its `WindowManager` above the `View` (`RunWidget`), so closing the first window with another open keeps the app running.
- **Main files:** `widgets/{window_controller,view,binding}.go`, `ui/platform_dispatcher.go`, `gluttertest/tester.go`, `examples/multiwindow/`, `internal/engine/first_window_display_test.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§8.7, §12.10), `docs/GUIDE.md`.
- **Tests:** `widgets/implicit_window_close_test.go`: the close request of the first window reaches the delegate with its controller and view, or is an exit request without one (3 cases, the delegate that keeps the window and the one that destroys it); a delegate taken away; destroying the first window with another open (states disposed, view gone from the dispatcher, content gone, the second window drawn and changed after), the delegate told once, a window closed by the platform, and destroying it alone; the multiwindow example's test (closing the first window keeps the second, which still works). Flutter test cases ported: 0 (the implicit window is Glutter's).
- **Display tests:** `TestDisplayTheFirstWindowCanBeDestroyedWhileOthersGoOn` runs the whole framework on the real engine, in a process of its own, on headless sway and on Xvfb: two windows, the first destroyed from a posted function, the second keeps drawing (10 frames, with a driver that asks for a frame every 10 ms) with the first's states disposed, then the second is destroyed and `Run` returns by itself. The Wayland, X11 and engine display suites pass.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · display tests ✅
- **Proof:** none.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - **Decided:** a method on the owner, not a `RunAppOpts` field, so the app can change the delegate while it runs. The windows that must outlive the first one cannot be below its `View`: with `RunApp` that is only so when a `WindowManager` is above the `View`, so an app that wants to close its first window uses `RunWidget` with a `WindowManager` around `WrapWithDefaultView` (the example does; GUIDE and SPEC §12.10 say so). `RunApp` itself is unchanged.
  - The unmounting at the end of a `gluttertest` test (27.2) now pumps a `ViewCollection` of no views with no `View` around it: with the implicit view gone, a `SizedBox` in a `View` panicked with `ImplicitViewMissing` (found by the new tests).
  - `TestRunTwiceFails` of the Wayland package failed once in a combined display run with `TempDir: mkdir /tmp/...: no such file or directory` (seen a second time earlier, in a repeated run): the temp directory disappears under the test, which is not related to this step; it passed in three more runs of the package.

## 27.8 `Draggable` and `DragTarget` for lists and tabs

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-27.8-draggable
- **Summary:** `MultiDragGestureRecognizerOpts.Slop` and `DraggableOpts.Slop` (`Opt[float64]`) set the distance before a drag starts, for every kind of pointer (the default stays `ComputeHitSlop`); `MultiDragPointerState.HitSlop()` is the one in use. `DraggableOpts.CancelOnEscape` adds a `HardwareKeyboard` handler for as long as the drag runs: Escape cancels it like a cancelled pointer (`OnDraggableCanceled`, `OnLeave` of the targets, the feedback removed) and is handled; the avatar ignores the moves and the release that follow. `DragTargetOpts.RepeatMove` calls `OnMove` once per frame while a drag is over the target even when the pointer rests; the avatar hit tests again on those frames, and requests a frame only while it is over such a target.
- **Main files:** `gestures/multidrag.go`, `widgets/drag_target.go`, `widgets/drag_target_options_test.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10).
- **Tests:** `widgets/drag_target_options_test.go`: a draggable row with a tap in it: a mouse moving 3 px with a slop of 4 is a click, 5 px is a drag, 3 px with the default slop is a drag, and the same for touch (5 cases); Escape during a drag, another key, and Escape with no option (3 cases, with the release after the cancel); the handler gone after the drag; `RepeatMove` calls per frame, none without the option or off the target, and no frame request or callback left over (3 cases); the hit test of a `Listener` above a plain list, a list in a `RawScrollbar`, in an opaque and in a non-opaque `MouseRegion` (5 cases).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - Task 4 (the hit test of a list under a `Listener`): Glutter does not differ from Flutter. `RenderMouseRegion.HitTest` is `super.hitTest && opaque` in both, so a **non-opaque** `MouseRegion` reports "not hit" to what is above it, in Flutter as well; the report's premise ("Flutter reports a hit when a child was hit") does not hold for that case. Nothing in `Scrollable`, `ListView` or `RawScrollbar` builds a non-opaque region (`RawScrollbar`'s is the default opaque one), and a deferring `Listener` above a plain list, or a list in a scrollbar or an opaque region, gets the press: the tests show it. An app that puts its own non-opaque `MouseRegion` around its rows has to give the `Listener` `HitTestBehaviorOpaque` or `Translucent`. No code change.
  - A `LongPressDraggable` takes `Slop` too: it is the slop within which the pointer may move before the delay passes.

## 27.9 `TreeSliver`: changing children, lazy nodes, node identity

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-27.9-tree-sliver
- **Summary:** `TreeSliverNode` has `InsertChild`, `RemoveChild` and `SetChildren` (and `AddChild` now tells the tree too): each node that is active holds a callback to the `TreeSliver`, which makes the active nodes again (so `Parent()` and `Depth()` are right, a removed node has none), ends the animations of nodes that left or lost their children, and collapses a node that has no children. `TreeSliverNodeOpts.HasChildren` and `HasChildren()` make a lazy node: it toggles with no children, `OnNodeToggle` is where the app sets them, and they show with the toggle animation (children that come later show at once); the default node builder shows its arrow. `TreeSliverOpts.NodeKey` makes `GetNodeFor` and `IsExpanded` compare keys, and keeps the expansion of the nodes whose key was in the tree before when it is built with new node objects.
- **Main files:** `widgets/sliver_tree.go`, `widgets/sliver_tree_nodes_test.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§12.10).
- **Tests:** the cases of `sliver_tree_test.go` pass as before. `widgets/sliver_tree_nodes_test.go`: ten changes of the children of a folder (insert at the start, the middle, beyond the end and before the start, add, remove one, remove a node that is not a child, remove all, replace, clear) with the rows, the parent, the depth and the expansion; a subtree moved and an expanded folder removed; changes during a toggle animation (remove the folder, replace its children, clear them); lazy nodes (children set in `OnNodeToggle` and the rows below moving during the animation, collapse and reopening, children that come after the toggle, a lazy node that starts expanded, a leaf that is not toggled and has no arrow); `NodeKey` in `GetNodeFor` and `IsExpanded` (4 cases, with and without it), the expansion across a tree of new nodes (with and without it), and a new node in a tree whose old folder was animating.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none.
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - A node removed with `RemoveChild` or dropped by `SetChildren` loses its `Parent()` and `Depth()`; a node that is moved is added to the new parent first and removed from the old one after (the other order collapses the old parent if it was its last child).
  - `NodeKey` keys are compared with `==` as map keys, so a key that cannot be compared panics, as a Go map does. The animations of the old nodes end when the tree is built with new node objects, rather than moving to the new ones.
  - Lazy nodes whose children are set after the toggle (an asynchronous read) show them at once, without the animation.

## 27.10 Cold start: what the first draw costs, and a shader cache

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-27.10-cold-start
- **Summary:** (1) With `GLUTTER_FRAME_STATS=1` the startup log splits the first draw: each renderer tried that failed (`stage="renderer tried"`, its error and time), then for the renderer chosen the first frame, the GPU context or device, the shaders (`built`, `from_cache`, `refused`, `pipeline_cache_bytes`) and the frame itself. A renderer reports its parts through `gpu.StartupReporter` (`gles.Renderer`, `explicit.Renderer` over the Vulkan device). (2) GLES: a program cache with `glGetProgramBinary`/`glProgramBinary` in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/glutter/shaders`, keyed by the hash of the driver strings, the program's name and its sources; a refused binary is compiled again and replaced; an unwritable cache is logged once and ignored; none on the web. (3) Vulkan: a `VkPipelineCache` per device in the same directory, loaded when the header is the device's (vendor, device, UUID), saved after the first frame and at close, only when it grew and is valid. (4) The programs and pipelines were already made at their first use (nothing is compiled ahead except by `CompileAll` in tests): a test shows that a first frame makes a few of them. (5) The cold start was measured with the new `scripts/perf.sh` (three states of the caches, and the parts of the first draw) and recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
- **Main files:** `internal/gpu/shadercache/`, `internal/gpu/startup.go`, `internal/gpu/gles/{device,renderer,glapi,gl_purego,gl_js,glconst}.go`, `internal/gpu/vulkan/{pipeline_cache,device,resources,vk,structs,consts,choose}.go`, `internal/gpu/explicit/renderer.go`, `internal/engine/{renderers,gles_renderer,backends_linux,engine}.go`, `scripts/perf.sh`, `docs/{SPEC,PERFORMANCE}.md` (§9.7), `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Tests:** `shadercache`: the directory from the environment (5), store and load (6: a miss, a hit, another key, a replace, empty data, a key that looks like a path), a directory that cannot be made or written (2, with routes `Cache.Store.ShaderCacheWriteFailed` and the reported-once rule), an unreadable file (`Cache.Load.ShaderCacheReadFailed`), no report function. `gles` over the fake GL: the cache across runs (5 cases: compile and store then load, only the programs used, a refused binary compiled again and replaced, another driver, a driver with no binary formats), a changed source, a short file, the files of the real cache, an unwritable cache (reported once), the startup report, and only the programs of the frame being made. `vulkan`: the header check (9 cases), the key (4), and the struct layout of `VkPipelineCacheCreateInfo` against `vulkan_core.h`. `explicit`: the cache saved once after the first frame, and the report. `engine`: the parts in the log (4 cases), the cache directory choice (4), the failure logged once with its tag.
- **Display tests:** `TestDisplayASecondStartFindsEveryProgramInTheCache` (headless sway: the first start builds 4 programs and writes 4 files, the second finds 4 of 4 in the cache, 0 built, 0 refused; the log says it), `TestDisplayTheCacheOff`, and `TestPipelineCacheSurvivesAClose` (the first Vulkan GPU of the machine, offscreen: loads what was saved, refuses another vendor's header, replaces the file; skipped on a CPU device).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · errcheck ✅ · apicheck ✅ · `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build, vet and `scripts/test-wasm.sh` ✅ · `scripts/check-android.sh` ✅ · display tests ✅
- **Proof:** none.
- **Manual checks:** the cold start of `examples/counter` with the GPU, `scripts/perf.sh` in the user's session (a headless compositor cannot present GPU buffers): **not done**, to be run on the desktop and recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. The numbers here are from llvmpipe (GLES) and the machine's AMD GPU (the Vulkan try that fails on the headless compositor).
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - **Needs the user's decision:** the failed Vulkan try of `auto` costs about 600 ms of a 960 ms cold start on a headless compositor (320 ms with `GLUTTER_RENDERER=gles`). Should `auto` try GLES first where Vulkan presents to no output? Not changed: SPEC §9.6 says Vulkan first.
  - On Mesa the shader cache buys almost nothing over Mesa's own disk cache (4 programs: 56 ms compiled with Mesa's cache warm, 42 ms loaded); the cold start falls from 3.6 s to 0.3 s because of Mesa's cache, which Glutter's start also fills. The cache is for the drivers that keep nothing; it is kept because the plan asks for it and costs a file per program.
  - lavapipe's `vkGetPipelineCacheData` gives a header that is cut short (20 bytes), so a Vulkan pipeline cache on a CPU device is never saved (the header is checked before saving).
  - Android keeps no shader cache yet (no `HOME`; the app's cache directory is not wired), and the web has none.
  - `SPEC` numbering: the new section is §9.7 (there was none).
  - **A flaky display test of step 27.5 was fixed (the test, not the engine).** `TestDisplayTheFirstWindowCanBeDestroyedWhileOthersGoOn` failed about 4 runs in 10 with `eglMakeCurrent failed` (`EGL_BAD_ACCESS`, 0x3002) after the first window's surface was released, with or without this step's changes. Cause: the three child tests that call `engine.Run` from a test goroutine did not pin it to an OS thread. `RunApp` runs on the main goroutine, which `internal/platform` keeps on the main thread (SPEC §8.1), but a test goroutine may move to another thread between frames, and EGL refuses a context that is current on the thread it left. The children now call `runtime.LockOSThread()`; 0 failures in 20 runs on sway, and the whole engine display set passes on sway (3 runs) and on Xvfb. The run of step 27.5 passed by luck. The failing child now also prints the error's route and metadata.

## 28.3 Mouse, touch, pen and cursors

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-28.3-windows-pointer
- **Summary:** Pointer input on Windows as Flutter's embedder delivers it.
  - Classic mouse messages: the buttons including the side ones, signed 16-bit coordinates, capture on the first button down and release on the last up, `WM_MOUSELEAVE`, and a capture lost to another window.
  - The wheel: vertical and horizontal, the system's lines setting, `WHEEL_PAGESCROLL`, precision touchpads.
  - Touch and pen from `WM_POINTER*`: one batch per frame, ids, pressure, tilt, rotation, the eraser end, the barrel button. A handled message never reaches `DefWindowProc`, and the system's touch and pen feedback is turned off.
  - The cursors of `SystemMouseCursors`, through `WM_SETCURSOR` and `MouseCursorNone`.
  - `GLUTTER_DEV_EVENTS` has `move`, `tap` and `wheel`, sent as real window messages.
  - One `pointerTracker`, a port of `FlutterWindowsView`'s pointer state, makes the final `ui.PointerData` for all of them.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/platform/windows/`: `pointerstate.go`, `mouse.go`, `wheel.go`, `pointer.go`, `idgen.go`, `cursor.go`, `devevents.go`, `input_windows.go`, `window_windows.go`, `platform_windows.go`
  - `internal/platform/windows/win32/`: `consts_input.go`, `structs_input.go`, `input_windows.go`, `layout_test.go`
  - `examples/counter/wine_input_test.go`, `examples/scrolling/wine_test.go`
  - `docs/SPEC.md` (§25.6, §12.10)
- **Tests:** about 200 table rows on the host and under Wine.
  - The tracker.
  - The mouse translator: a click, a drag outside with capture, a leave during a drag, two buttons, side buttons, capture taken by another window.
  - The wheel.
  - The touch and pen translator over recorded values: several contacts in one frame, tilt, rotation, the eraser, hover, a lost capture.
  - The id generator, the cursor table (every name of `SystemMouseCursors`), the struct sizes.
  - 22 Flutter test cases ported: 16 of `flutter_window_unittests.cc`, 3 of `window_unittests.cc` (`VerticalScroll`, `HorizontalScroll`, `MouseLeave`), 2 of `sequential_id_generator_unittests.cc`, `ActivateSystemCursor` of `cursor_handler_unittests.cc`, and the table of `GetCursorByName`. `flutter_windows_view_unittests.cc` has no pointer case at the pinned commit; the DirectManipulation and custom-cursor cases are not ported.
- **Wine tests:**
  - In the window process, with `SendInput` after `SetCursorPos`:
    - three clicks are 3 downs and 3 ups, and two buttons work together;
    - a drag released outside the window ends in a real up;
    - `WM_MOUSELEAVE` removes the pointer;
    - the capture taken by another window gives a synthesized up;
    - the wheel scrolls by the system's lines setting;
    - the scripted events work;
    - `GetCursorInfo` shows the cursors of the table, and `WM_SETCURSOR` answers as it should;
    - a destroyed window cancels its pointers.
  - Host-side:
    - the counter after three scripted taps shows the same text as `GLUTTER_DEV_TAPS=3`, pixel for pixel;
    - `examples/scrolling` after a scripted wheel of 400 pixels shows the same content as `GLUTTER_DEV_SCROLL=400`, pixel for pixel.

  ![28.3](implemented-proof-images/28.3-windows-scrolling.png)
- **Manual checks: pending**, collected in `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md` by step 28.15:
  - all mouse buttons including the side ones, and a drag outside the window;
  - a notched and a free-spinning wheel;
  - a precision touchpad with two-finger scroll and pinch;
  - a touch screen;
  - a pen with pressure, the eraser end and the barrel button;
  - the cursors in the gallery.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - The platform makes the final `PointerData`; the engine's `PointerDataPacketConverter` has no counterpart (SPEC §12.10). So:
    - a move with no button down ends the contact;
    - a pointer that leaves while down is lifted first;
    - a leave for a pointer never added is ignored;
    - each down gets a new `PointerIdentifier`.
  - The first button of any kind takes the capture (Flutter: the left button only).
  - Pen pressure is 0 to 1 (Flutter: 0 to 1024); a pen in the air has pressure 0.
  - The wheel's lines setting is read at each message, and `WHEEL_PAGESCROLL` is a page of the view.
  - Cursors with no stock counterpart take the nearest one: `grab` and `grabbing` the hand; `zoomIn`, `zoomOut` and `cell` the cross; `verticalText` the I-beam; `copy`, `alias`, `contextMenu` and `disappearing` the arrow.
  - Wine sends `WM_MOUSELEAVE` for a captured pointer at once, Windows only after the release. So a leave during a drag waits for the last button up.
  - Touch and pen `WM_POINTER` messages cannot be made under Wine: they are tested as plain Go, and the devices are manual checks.
  - The layout tests of the new mirrors (`POINTER_INFO`, `POINTER_TOUCH_INFO`, `POINTER_PEN_INFO`, `INPUT`) still skip, because `mingw64-gcc` and `mingw64-headers` are not installed. Until then, `TestInputStructSizes` checks hand-computed sizes and offsets.
  - Not done:
    - custom cursors (`createCustomCursor`);
    - DirectManipulation (SPEC §25.6: no `PointerPanZoom` on Windows in 1.8);
    - modifier sync on mouse move (step 28.4).

## 28.4 Keyboard

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-28.4-windows-keyboard
- **Summary:** Windows keys are now reported to the framework the way Flutter's embedder reports them, on any keyboard layout.
  - `glutter-gen keys -windows-out` writes the key tables from Flutter's key data into `internal/platform/windows/keymap_gen.go`. The file header names the pinned Flutter commit.
  - A plain-Go converter (port of `KeyboardKeyEmbedderHandler`) and manager (port of `KeyboardManager`) turn the key messages and the queued character messages into key data:
    - key messages: `WM_KEYDOWN`, `WM_KEYUP`, `WM_SYSKEYDOWN`, `WM_SYSKEYUP`;
    - synthesized modifier and lock events, and repeats;
    - the fake left Control that comes with AltGr is dropped;
    - held keys are released on `WM_KILLFOCUS`, and the lock states are read again on `WM_SETFOCUS`.
  - `DefaultTextEditingShortcutMap()` gives the Windows map on Windows.
  - `GLUTTER_DEV_EVENTS` gains `key:`, `keydown:` and `keyup:`, sent with `SendInput`.
- **Main files:**
  - `cmd/glutter-gen/internal/keys/windows.go`
  - `internal/platform/windows/`: `keyboard.go`, `keymanager.go`, `deadkeys.go`, `keyboard_windows.go`, `keymap_gen.go`, `devevents.go`
  - `internal/platform/windows/win32/`: `consts_key.go`, `key_windows.go`, `structs_input.go`
  - `widgets/default_text_editing_shortcuts.go`
  - SPEC §11.1, §12.10, §25.6
- **Tests:**
  - About 75 table cases adapted from about 30 tests of `keyboard_unittests.cc`, `keyboard_key_embedder_handler_unittests.cc` and `keyboard_key_handler_unittests.cc`. The redispatching, channel and Telex tests are not ported.
  - The generated tables equal the three maps of `flutter_key_map.g.cc`, plus 42 spot checks.
  - The generator, over fixtures with 10 route-tested failures and over the real data (157 physical and 121 logical keys).
  - The Windows cases of `default_text_editing_shortcuts_test.dart` and `editable_text_shortcuts_test.dart`.
  - The layout test against the mingw-w64 headers now really runs (`mingw64-gcc` is installed). It covers the new `KEYBDINPUT` and the 66 new constants, and its first run found `QS_ALLINPUT` wrong (see below).
- **Wine tests:**
  - Keys typed with `SendInput` give the right key data in order: letters, Shift, Backspace, Delete, the arrows, Home, End, Page Down, Return, Space, Control+A, Escape.
  - A held key repeats; held keys are released when the window loses focus; the lock states are seen after the focus returns.
  - Alt alone does not open the system menu, Alt+Space does, and Alt+F4 closes the window.

- **Proof:** method F, `docs/implemented-proof-images/28.4-windows-editor.png`. It shows `examples/editor` under Wine after scripted keys: "Hello world", a new line, "Typed with keys", then Shift+Control+Left twice to select "with keys". The status bar reads "Ln 2, Col 7 (9 selected)".

  ![28.4](implemented-proof-images/28.4-windows-editor.png)
- **Manual checks (pending, for the owner's PC; collected in `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md` by step 28.15):**
  - a German or French layout and a Russian or Greek one;
  - AltGr characters and dead keys;
  - the numpad;
  - Windows-key combinations;
  - Alt+F4, Alt+Space and F10;
  - key repeat;
  - switching layouts with Win+Space while the app runs.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - Six new rows in SPEC §12.10:
    - a dead key has no character, and every character message after a key down is part of that key's text;
    - the fake left Control of AltGr is dropped;
    - the answers to system keys;
    - keys are released and lock states read again when the focus changes;
    - layout goals apply on Windows;
    - the character messages are always taken.
  - The SPEC §25.6 sentence on AltGr is corrected: Flutter forwards the fake Control and forges its key up.
  - Wine ignores a loaded keyboard layout, so the German half of the layout-goal Wine test skips. Recorded answers stand in for it.
  - Control+C, X and V are not tested yet: they need the Windows clipboard of step 28.6.
  - Fixed in this step: `win32.QSAllInput` was `0x04FF`, which lacks `QS_TOUCH` and `QS_POINTER`. The message loop would not have woken for queued touch and pen messages from step 28.3. It is now `0x1CFF`, found by the layout test.
  - Found, not changed (same as Flutter): the actions that move by the layout use the value of the last laid-out frame. These are the page actions (Page Up, Page Down), the line-break actions (Home, End) and the word actions. A Page Down in the same turn as typing puts the old text back, and a Shift+End right after a Delete selects nothing. The scripted events therefore need a `wait:` between an edit and such a key, and the editor test has one; without it, the test failed or passed depending on timing. Typing at human speed always has a frame in between.

## 28.5 Text input and IMEs

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-28.5-windows-ime
- **Summary:** Text fields on Windows now work with the input methods. The composition is drawn in the field, and the candidate window follows the caret.
  - `internal/platform/windows/ime` is a plain-Go model over a small `IMM` interface. `imm_windows.go` calls imm32, and `imetest` is a fake of it.
  - The IME messages become `TextInputEvent`s through `textedit.TextEditor`:
    - `WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION` and `WM_IME_ENDCOMPOSITION`;
    - `WM_IME_COMPOSITION`: `GCS_COMPSTR` with `GCS_CURSORPOS` is the preedit, and `GCS_RESULTSTR` is the commit;
    - `WM_IME_SETCONTEXT` hides the system composition window.
  - A `WM_CHAR` that no key made is typed, with surrogate pairs. It comes from an input method or from `SendInput` with `KEYEVENTF_UNICODE`.
  - `SetTextInput` turns the IME on while a text field has the focus and off otherwise. It keeps the composition window, the candidate window and the system caret at the scaled caret rectangle.
  - `GLUTTER_DEV_EVENTS` gains `text:`, `compose:` and `composing:`. They are sent as real window messages, and only the strings of the input context come from the script.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/platform/windows/ime/`
  - `internal/platform/windows/`: `textinput_windows.go`, `devevents.go`, `window_windows.go`, `keyboard_windows.go`
  - `internal/platform/windows/win32/`: `imm_windows.go`, `consts_ime.go`, `structs_ime.go`
  - SPEC §12.10, §25.6, §25.7
- **Tests:**
  - `ime` over the fake IMM, covering 96% of statements:
    - Japanese and Chinese sessions, a cancel, an emptied string;
    - a result and a new composing string in one message, a selection replaced by the first preedit;
    - surrogate pairs and combining marks, a missing or invalid caret position, characters;
    - a composition across a framework state change, the IME on and off, the abort when the field goes away;
    - the candidate window placement at scales 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2.
  - Ported from Flutter:
    - the 7 `OnImeComposition*` cases of `window_unittests.cc`;
    - `CompositionCursorPos` and `VerifyComposingSendStateUpdate` of `text_input_plugin_unittest.cc`, with the behavior of 3 more cases tested;
    - the Telex case and the end of the submit case of `keyboard_unittests.cc`, and the `VK_PROCESSKEY` case.
  - The `COMPOSITIONFORM` and `CANDIDATEFORM` mirrors and 30 constants are checked against the mingw-w64 headers.
- **Wine tests:**
  - The input context follows the field: `ImmAssociateContext(NULL)` turns the IME off and back on.
  - `ImmGetCandidateWindow`, `ImmGetCompositionWindow` and `GetCaretPos` give the caret rectangle and follow it.
  - Scripted text and compositions arrive as `Preedit` and `Commit`.

## 28.6 Clipboard, settings, fonts and lifecycle

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-28.6-windows-clipboard-settings
- **Summary:**
  - **Clipboard:** copy and paste work on Windows for text, files and images (`CF_UNICODETEXT`, `CF_HDROP`, `PNG` and `CF_DIBV5`). A busy clipboard is retried, and reads run on a thread of their own with the context.
  - **Settings:** the app follows the system's settings live on `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`:
    - dark or light app mode, applied to the title bars of every window;
    - accent color, high contrast, text size and animations;
    - locales, the 24-hour clock and the UI fonts;
    - the caret blink time and the double-click time, now in `Settings` and `ui.PlatformConfiguration`. `EditableText` blinks at the system's rate, and not at all when the system says never.
  - **Fonts:** text uses the system's fonts through the new `internal/text/winfonts` matcher, with the generic families and a fallback chain by script and language. It is plugged into `engine.SystemFontMatcher`.
  - **Lifecycle:** the app follows Windows' lifecycle (Resumed, Inactive, Hidden, Detached). While it is Hidden, no frames are drawn. The end of the session ends `Run`.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/platform/windows/`: `clipboard.go`, `clipboard_windows.go`, `settings.go`, `settings_windows.go`, `lifecycle.go`, `lifecycle_windows.go`, `fonts.go`, `fonts_windows.go`

## 28.7 Shaders for Direct3D 12

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-28.7-d3d12-shaders
- **Summary:**
  - **HLSL generation:** `glutter-gen shaders` now also writes the HLSL (shader model 5.1) of every shader into `shaders_gen.go`, as `Shader.HLSL` with `ShaderBinding.Register` per binding.
  - **The sampler rewrite:** naga 30.0.1's command line cannot place samplers: it writes a sampler heap with index buffers in `space255`. By the owner's decision (2026-10-25), the generator rewrites naga's HLSL into plain `register(sB, spaceG)` declarations, so every binding sits at `register(<class>B, spaceG)` and Resource Binding Tier 1 hardware keeps working. The generator fails on any shape it does not know, and checks every register against the WGSL.
  - **Rotation:** the blit's pre-rotation moved from the first instance to a uniform on every backend, because Direct3D's `SV_InstanceID` does not include the first instance.
  - **The `internal/gpu/d3d12` package:** it compiles each entry point with `D3DCompile` from `d3dcompiler_47.dll` and keeps the DXBC in the shader cache. The cache key is the HLSL, the entry point, the target, the flags and the compiler's file version. It reads the registers back with `D3DReflect`.
- **Main files:**
  - `cmd/glutter-gen/internal/shaders/`: `hlsl.go`, `shaders.go`
  - `internal/gpu/explicit/`: `shader.go`, `shaders_gen.go`, `shaders/blit.wgsl`, `renderer.go`, `scene.go`
  - `internal/gpu/d3d12/`: `doc.go`, `compiler.go`, `hlslcache.go`, `types.go`, `compile_windows.go`, `reflect_windows.go`
  - `internal/platform/windows/win32/`: `version_windows.go`, `structs_version.go`, `mem_windows.go`
  - SPEC §9.8 and §24.5, and `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md` steps 28.7 and 28.9
- **Tests:**
  - **Generator:**
    - the rewrite over a real naga fixture, with every kind of binding, two groups and comparison samplers;

  - **Renderer (`explicit`):** `TestGeneratedHLSL` and `TestEveryDrawStartsAtTheFirstVertexAndInstance`. The rotation tests were updated for the uniform.
  - **`d3d12`:**
    - each part of the cache key, and `ValidDXBC`;
    - the cache over a directory: hit, miss, bad header, unwritable directory, no cache;
    - the compile flags;
    - a route test of `D3D12ShaderCompileFailed`;
